entries.label: sem:SpectralSequence:bounded-ess
entries.title: The bounded extension spectral sequence
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body: For the same filtered map $f$, assume that both actual filtrations are bounded. Its extension spectral sequence begins on page zero and has differential degree $(n,-1)$ at page $n$ in the grading of the two-term complex. Its source and target ambient objects are the corresponding associated graded pieces of the original filtrations.

comments.title: Interface scope: bounded-extension-sequence
comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `bounded-extension-sequence`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: Obtain the extension spectral sequence of the same bounded filtered map and connect its actual differentials to the extension equation.

- **interface_role**: A small opaque public construction and proved comparison interface around the private filtered complex.

- **mathematical_strength_preserved**: Both source and target degreewise boundedness witnesses are explicit and belong to the very same filtrations as f.

- **mathematical_strength_preserved**: The supplied sequence starts at zero and has differential degree (n,-1). sourceIso and targetIso identify its actual ambient objects with the source/target associated grades.

- **mathematical_strength_preserved**: For n : ℕ and Projective T, differentialRelation_iff equates the actual differential relation of this sequence with Relation f, after the specified isomorphisms.

- **mathematical_strength_preserved**: The bridge is proved via the original FilteredComplex.Solutions.Fiber equivalence, retaining its actual-lift semantics and projectivity condition.

- **boundary**: No unbounded ESS construction is asserted. General extension relations remain usable without boundedness.

- **boundary**: No direct current AdamsSynthetic use of sequence is claimed: that module consumes the general extension equation; the bounded ESS bridge is exercised by the ordinary-import SpectralSequence consumer test.

- **boundary**: FilteredComplex, underlyingComplex, solution-fiber implementation and their construction proofs remain private.

entries.label: sem:SpectralSequence:ess-equation
entries.title: ESS differentials are extension equations
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body: For bounded source and target filtrations, a nonnegative length $n$, and a projective test object, the actual differential relation in the bounded extension spectral sequence is equivalent to the representative extension equation for the original filtered map.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapExtension.differentialRelation_iff
lean.code:
public theorem differentialRelation_iff (f : FilteredMorphism F G)
    (hF : F.IsBounded) (hG : G.IsBounded) (k : ω) (s : ℤ) (n : ℕ)
    {T : C} [Projective T] (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded s k)
    (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded (s + (n : ℤ)) k) :
    DifferentialRelation (sequence f hF hG k) n (s, 1)
      (x ≫ (sourceIso f hF hG k s).inv)
      (y ≫ (targetIso f hF hG k s n).inv) ↔ Relation f k s n x y := by
  rw [relation_iff_fiber, and_iff_right (Int.natCast_nonneg n)]
  change DifferentialRelation
    ((underlyingComplex f.map f.compat k).toSpectralSequence
      (underlyingComplexBounded f.map f.compat k hF hG)) n (s, 1)
    (x ≫ 𝟙 (F.associatedGraded s k)) (y ≫ 𝟙 (G.associatedGraded (s + ↑n) k)) ↔ _
  rw [Category.comp_id, Category.comp_id]
  exact
    FilteredComplex.Solutions.differentialRelation_iff_nonempty_fiber
      (underlyingComplex f.map f.compat k)
      (underlyingComplexBounded f.map f.compat k hF hG) n s 1 x y
lean.statement:
public theorem differentialRelation_iff (f : FilteredMorphism F G)
    (hF : F.IsBounded) (hG : G.IsBounded) (k : ω) (s : ℤ) (n : ℕ)
    {T : C} [Projective T] (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded s k)
    (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded (s + (n : ℤ)) k) :
    DifferentialRelation (sequence f hF hG k) n (s, 1)
      (x ≫ (sourceIso f hF hG k s).inv)
      (y ≫ (targetIso f hF hG k s n).inv) ↔ Relation f k s n x y
lean.docstring:
The actual ESS differential relation is precisely the original filtered-map
equation. Projectivity is retained when arbitrary morphism-valued labels are used.

entries.label: sem:SpectralSequence:filtered-transport
entries.title: Transport by levelwise filtered isomorphisms
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body: A filtered-piece isomorphism identifies the ambient objects and every filtration level, compatibly with inclusion. A transport of filtered maps consists of such isomorphisms on source and target making the actual ambient square commute.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapTransport

public structure FilteredMapTransport (f : FilteredMorphism F G)
    (f' : FilteredMorphism F' G') (k : ω) (k' : ω') where
  source : FilteredPieceIso F F' k k'
  target : FilteredPieceIso G G' k k'
  map_comm : source.ambient.hom ≫ f'.map k' = f.map k ≫ target.ambient.hom

A commuting square between the actual filtered maps, together with

entries.label: sem:SpectralSequence:extension-transport
entries.title: Transport preserves extensions and their full ambiguity
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body: Levelwise filtered transport preserves representative equations, extension relations, complete target indeterminacy, target cosets, and essentiality. These representative-level statements do not require bounded filtrations.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapTransport.representative_equation_iff
lean.code:
public theorem representative_equation_iff
    (a : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (F.F s k))
    (b : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (G.F (s+n) k)) :
    a ≫ (F.F s k).arrow ≫ f.map k = b ≫ (G.F (s+n) k).arrow ↔
      (a ≫ (e.source.level s).hom) ≫ (F'.F s k').arrow ≫ f'.map k' =
        (b ≫ (e.target.level (s+n)).hom) ≫ (G'.F (s+n) k').arrow := by
  have hsource := e.source.level_arrow s
  have htarget := e.target.level_arrow (s+n)
  simp only [Category.assoc]
  rw [← Category.assoc (e.source.level s).hom, hsource, Category.assoc, e.map_comm]
  rw [htarget]
  constructor
  · intro h
    simpa only [Category.assoc] using congrArg (fun z => z ≫ e.target.ambient.hom) h
  · intro h
    apply (cancel_mono e.target.ambient.hom).mp
    simpa only [Category.assoc] using h
lean.statement:
public theorem representative_equation_iff
    (a : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (F.F s k))
    (b : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (G.F (s+n) k)) :
    a ≫ (F.F s k).arrow ≫ f.map k = b ≫ (G.F (s+n) k).arrow ↔
      (a ≫ (e.source.level s).hom) ≫ (F'.F s k').arrow ≫ f'.map k' =
        (b ≫ (e.target.level (s+n)).hom) ≫ (G'.F (s+n) k').arrow
lean.docstring: The chosen representatives transport along the actual level isomorphisms.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapTransport.relation_iff
lean.code:
public theorem relation_iff
    (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded s k)
    (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded (s+n) k) :
    FilteredMapExtension.Relation f k s n x y ↔
      FilteredMapExtension.Relation f' k' s n
        (x ≫ (e.source.gradedIso s).hom) (y ≫ (e.target.gradedIso (s+n)).hom) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hn, a, b, ha, hb, he⟩
    refine ⟨hn, a ≫ (e.source.level s).hom,
      b ≫ (e.target.level (s+n)).hom, ?_, ?_,
      (e.representative_equation_iff a b).mp he⟩
    · rw [Category.assoc, ← e.source.projection_comm, ← Category.assoc, ha]
    · rw [Category.assoc, ← e.target.projection_comm, ← Category.assoc, hb]
  · rintro ⟨hn, a, b, ha, hb, he⟩
    refine ⟨hn, a ≫ (e.source.level s).inv,
      b ≫ (e.target.level (s+n)).inv, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Category.assoc, ← e.source.projection_inv_comm, ← Category.assoc, ha]
      simp
    · rw [Category.assoc, ← e.target.projection_inv_comm, ← Category.assoc, hb]
      simp
    · apply (e.representative_equation_iff _ _).mpr
      simpa using he

        FilteredMapExtension.TargetIndeterminacy f' k' s n T := by

public theorem essential_iff (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded s k)
    (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded (s+n) k) :

      FilteredMapExtension.Essential f' k' s n

  rw [e.relation_iff]

entries.label: sem:SpectralSequence:crossing-transport
entries.title: Transport of crossings and ESS differentials
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body: A crossing is a higher-source-filtration essential extension whose target level crosses the selected bound. Such crossings are preserved by filtered transport. If all four filtrations are bounded and the test object is projective, transport also preserves the differential relation in the extension spectral sequences.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapTransport.noCrossing_iff
lean.code:
public theorem noCrossing_iff (s n : ℤ) (T : C) :
    NoCrossing f k s n T ↔ NoCrossing f' k' s n T := by
  apply not_congr
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨a, m, ha, hm, hmn, x, y, he⟩
    exact ⟨a, m, ha, hm, hmn, _, _, (e.essential_iff x y).mp he⟩
  · rintro ⟨a, m, ha, hm, hmn, x, y, he⟩
    refine ⟨a, m, ha, hm, hmn, x ≫ (e.source.gradedIso (s+a)).inv,
      y ≫ (e.target.gradedIso ((s+a)+m)).inv, ?_⟩
    apply (e.essential_iff _ _).mpr
    simpa using he
lean.statement:
public theorem noCrossing_iff (s n : ℤ) (T : C) :
    NoCrossing f k s n T ↔ NoCrossing f' k' s n T

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapTransport.NoCrossing
lean.code:
public def NoCrossing (f : FilteredMorphism F G) (k : ω) (s n : ℤ) (T : C) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (a m : ℤ), 0 < a ∧ 0 ≤ m ∧ a + m ≤ n ∧
    ∃ (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded (s+a) k)
      (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded ((s+a)+m) k),
      FilteredMapExtension.Essential f k (s+a) m x y

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapTransport.differentialRelation_iff
lean.code:
public theorem differentialRelation_iff
    (hF : F.IsBounded) (hG : G.IsBounded)
    (hF' : F'.IsBounded) (hG' : G'.IsBounded)
    (s : ℤ) (n : ℕ) [Projective T]
    (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded s k)
    (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded (s+(n:ℤ)) k) :
    DifferentialRelation (FilteredMapExtension.sequence f hF hG k) n (s,1)
      (x ≫ (FilteredMapExtension.sourceIso f hF hG k s).inv)
      (y ≫ (FilteredMapExtension.targetIso f hF hG k s n).inv) ↔
    DifferentialRelation (FilteredMapExtension.sequence f' hF' hG' k') n (s,1)
      (x ≫ (e.source.gradedIso s).hom ≫
        (FilteredMapExtension.sourceIso f' hF' hG' k' s).inv)
      (y ≫ (e.target.gradedIso (s+(n:ℤ))).hom ≫
        (FilteredMapExtension.targetIso f' hF' hG' k' s n).inv) := by
  rw [FilteredMapExtension.differentialRelation_iff]
  rw [← Category.assoc x, ← Category.assoc y,
    FilteredMapExtension.differentialRelation_iff]
  exact e.relation_iff x y

entries.label: sem:SpectralSequence:pairing
entries.title: Pairings of spectral sequences
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body: A pairing is bilinear on every page, has a specified parity and compatible differential degrees, obeys the signed Leibniz rule, and descends through the actual common-cycle successor-page relation.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.NextPageRelation
lean.code:
public def NextPageRelation {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (E : SpectralSequence (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ℤ × ℤ)) (r : ℤ)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) (x : E.Page r p) (y : E.Page (r + 1) p) : Prop :=
  let D := E.ssData p
  let n : WithTop ℕ := ↑(r - E.r₀).toNat
  let n' : WithTop ℕ := ↑(r + 1 - E.r₀).toNat
  ∃ z : (Subobject.underlying.obj (D.Z n') : ModuleCat R),
    (Subobject.ofLE (D.Z n') (D.Z n)
      (D.Z_anti (by
        change (↑(r - E.r₀).toNat : WithTop ℕ) ≤ ↑(r + 1 - E.r₀).toNat
        exact_mod_cast (show (r - E.r₀).toNat ≤ (r + 1 - E.r₀).toNat by omega))) ≫
      D.pageπ n) z = x ∧
      D.pageπ n' z = y

This uses one next-cycle representative for both quotient classes.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.SSPairing
lean.code:
public structure SSPairing (E₁ E₂ E₃ : SpectralSequence (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ℤ × ℤ)) where
  diffDeg_compatible : ∀ r : ℤ,
    E₁.diffDeg r = E₂.diffDeg r ∧ E₁.diffDeg r = E₃.diffDeg r
  parity : GradingParity
  pair : ∀ (r : ℤ) (k l : ℤ × ℤ),
    E₁.Page r k →ₗ[R] E₂.Page r l →ₗ[R] E₃.Page r (k + l)
  leibniz : ∀ (r : ℤ) (k l : ℤ × ℤ) (x : E₁.Page r k) (y : E₂.Page r l),
    E₃.d r (k + l) (pair r k l x y) =
      (transportPage E₃ r (by rw [(diffDeg_compatible r).2]; ac_rfl))
        (pair r (k + E₁.diffDeg r) l (E₁.d r k x) y) +
      (if parity k = 1 then (-1 : ℤ) else 1) •
        (transportPage E₃ r (by rw [← (diffDeg_compatible r).1, (diffDeg_compatible r).2]; ac_rfl))
          (pair r k (l + E₂.diffDeg r) x (E₂.d r l y))
  nextPage_compatible : ∀ (r : ℤ) (k l : ℤ × ℤ),
    E₁.r₀ ≤ r → E₂.r₀ ≤ r → E₃.r₀ ≤ r →
    ∀ (x : E₁.Page r k) (x' : E₁.Page (r + 1) k)
      (y : E₂.Page r l) (y' : E₂.Page (r + 1) l),
    NextPageRelation E₁ r k x x' → NextPageRelation E₂ r l y y' →
    NextPageRelation E₃ r (k + l) (pair r k l x y) (pair (r + 1) k l x' y')

entries.label: sem:SpectralSequence:converging-pairing
entries.title: Products from finite pages to the abutment
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body: A converging pairing ties the finite-page products to one product on common infinite cycles, its induced $E_\infty$ product, the filtered abutment product, and the associated graded product. All comparisons use the same convergence isomorphisms.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.ConvergingSSPairing
lean.code:
public structure ConvergingSSPairing
    (X₁ X₂ X₃ : ConvergingSS (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ℤ × ℤ) ℤ) where
  ssPairing : SSPairing X₁.E X₂.E X₃.E
  eInftyPair : ∀ k l : ℤ × ℤ,
    (X₁.E.ssData k).eInfty →ₗ[R] (X₂.E.ssData l).eInfty →ₗ[R]
      (X₃.E.ssData (k + l)).eInfty
  cyclePairAtInfinity : ∀ k l : ℤ × ℤ,
    InfiniteCycles X₁.E k →ₗ[R] InfiniteCycles X₂.E l →ₗ[R] InfiniteCycles X₃.E (k + l)
  eInftyPair_induced : ∀ (k l : ℤ × ℤ)
      (x : InfiniteCycles X₁.E k) (y : InfiniteCycles X₂.E l),
    (X₃.E.ssData (k + l)).pageπ ⊤ (cyclePairAtInfinity k l x y) =
      eInftyPair k l ((X₁.E.ssData k).pageπ ⊤ x) ((X₂.E.ssData l).pageπ ⊤ y)
  finitePagePair_compatible : ∀ (r : ℤ) (k l : ℤ × ℤ),
    X₁.E.r₀ ≤ r → X₂.E.r₀ ≤ r → X₃.E.r₀ ≤ r →
    ∀ (x : InfiniteCycles X₁.E k) (y : InfiniteCycles X₂.E l),
    ssPairing.pair r k l (infinityToPage X₁.E r k x) (infinityToPage X₂.E r l y) =
      infinityToPage X₃.E r (k + l) (cyclePairAtInfinity k l x y)
  abutmentPair : ∀ i j : ℤ, X₁.A i →ₗ[R] X₂.A j →ₗ[R] X₃.A (i + j)
  filteredAbutmentPair : ∀ s t i j : ℤ,
    FiltrationPiece X₁.F s i →ₗ[R] FiltrationPiece X₂.F t j →ₗ[R]
      FiltrationPiece X₃.F (s + t) (i + j)
  filteredAbutmentPair_compatible : ∀ (s t i j : ℤ)
      (x : FiltrationPiece X₁.F s i) (y : FiltrationPiece X₂.F t j),
    (X₃.F.F (s + t) (i + j)).arrow (filteredAbutmentPair s t i j x y) =
      abutmentPair i j ((X₁.F.F s i).arrow x) ((X₂.F.F t j).arrow y)
  associatedGradedPair : ∀ s t i j : ℤ,
    X₁.F.associatedGraded s i →ₗ[R] X₂.F.associatedGraded t j →ₗ[R]
      X₃.F.associatedGraded (s + t) (i + j)
  associatedGradedPair_induced : ∀ (s t i j : ℤ)
      (x : FiltrationPiece X₁.F s i) (y : FiltrationPiece X₂.F t j),
    associatedGradedPair s t i j (X₁.F.toAssociatedGraded s i x)
        (X₂.F.toAssociatedGraded t j y) =
      X₃.F.toAssociatedGraded (s + t) (i + j) (filteredAbutmentPair s t i j x y)
  reindex_compatible : ∀ k l : ℤ × ℤ,
    X₁.conv.reindex k + X₂.conv.reindex l = X₃.conv.reindex (k + l)
  eInfty_compatible : ∀ (k l : ℤ × ℤ)
      (x : (X₁.E.ssData k).eInfty) (y : (X₂.E.ssData l).eInfty),
    X₃.F.transportGraded (reindex_compatible k l).symm
      ((X₃.conv.iso (k + l)).hom (eInftyPair k l x y)) =
      associatedGradedPair (X₁.conv.reindex k).1 (X₂.conv.reindex l).1
        (X₁.conv.reindex k).2 (X₂.conv.reindex l).2
        ((X₁.conv.iso k).hom x) ((X₂.conv.iso l).hom y)

    (X₁ X₂ X₃ : ConvergingSS (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ℤ × ℤ) ℤ) where
  ssPairing : SSPairing X₁.E X₂.E X₃.E
  eInftyPair : ∀ k l : ℤ × ℤ,
    (X₁.E.ssData k).eInfty →ₗ[R] (X₂.E.ssData l).eInfty →ₗ[R]

  cyclePairAtInfinity : ∀ k l : ℤ × ℤ,
    InfiniteCycles X₁.E k →ₗ[R] InfiniteCycles X₂.E l →ₗ[R] InfiniteCycles X₃.E (k + l)
  eInftyPair_induced : ∀ (k l : ℤ × ℤ)
      (x : InfiniteCycles X₁.E k) (y : InfiniteCycles X₂.E l),
    (X₃.E.ssData (k + l)).pageπ ⊤ (cyclePairAtInfinity k l x y) =
      eInftyPair k l ((X₁.E.ssData k).pageπ ⊤ x) ((X₂.E.ssData l).pageπ ⊤ y)

    ∀ (x : InfiniteCycles X₁.E k) (y : InfiniteCycles X₂.E l),
    ssPairing.pair r k l (infinityToPage X₁.E r k x) (infinityToPage X₂.E r l y) =
      infinityToPage X₃.E r (k + l) (cyclePairAtInfinity k l x y)
  abutmentPair : ∀ i j : ℤ, X₁.A i →ₗ[R] X₂.A j →ₗ[R] X₃.A (i + j)
  filteredAbutmentPair : ∀ s t i j : ℤ,
    FiltrationPiece X₁.F s i →ₗ[R] FiltrationPiece X₂.F t j →ₗ[R]
      FiltrationPiece X₃.F (s + t) (i + j)
  filteredAbutmentPair_compatible : ∀ (s t i j : ℤ)
      (x : FiltrationPiece X₁.F s i) (y : FiltrationPiece X₂.F t j),
    (X₃.F.F (s + t) (i + j)).arrow (filteredAbutmentPair s t i j x y) =
      abutmentPair i j ((X₁.F.F s i).arrow x) ((X₂.F.F t j).arrow y)
  associatedGradedPair : ∀ s t i j : ℤ,
    X₁.F.associatedGraded s i →ₗ[R] X₂.F.associatedGraded t j →ₗ[R]
      X₃.F.associatedGraded (s + t) (i + j)
  associatedGradedPair_induced : ∀ (s t i j : ℤ)
      (x : FiltrationPiece X₁.F s i) (y : FiltrationPiece X₂.F t j),
    associatedGradedPair s t i j (X₁.F.toAssociatedGraded s i x)
        (X₂.F.toAssociatedGraded t j y) =
      X₃.F.toAssociatedGraded (s + t) (i + j) (filteredAbutmentPair s t i j x y)
  reindex_compatible : ∀ k l : ℤ × ℤ,
    X₁.conv.reindex k + X₂.conv.reindex l = X₃.conv.reindex (k + l)
  eInfty_compatible : ∀ (k l : ℤ × ℤ)
      (x : (X₁.E.ssData k).eInfty) (y : (X₂.E.ssData l).eInfty),
    X₃.F.transportGraded (reindex_compatible k l).symm
      ((X₃.conv.iso (k + l)).hom (eInftyPair k l x y)) =
      associatedGradedPair (X₁.conv.reindex k).1 (X₂.conv.reindex l).1
        (X₁.conv.reindex k).2 (X₂.conv.reindex l).2
        ((X₁.conv.iso k).hom x) ((X₂.conv.iso l).hom y)

entries.label: paper:2.1
entries.title: The extension spectral sequence
entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 2.1.)


  For a map $f: X\to Y$, we define an $f$-extension spectral sequence (denoted $f$-ESS) as the spectral sequence derived from filtering the above chain complex according to the Adams filtration on $\pi_*$. The $E_0$-page of this spectral sequence is isomorphic to the direct sum of $E_\infty$-pages of the Adams spectral sequences of $X$ and $Y$: 
  $$\ESS{f}_0^{s,t} \cong E_\infty^{s,t}(X) \oplus E_\infty^{s,t}(Y) \Longrightarrow \Ker(\pi_*f)\oplus \Coker(\pi_*f)$$
  where the $d_0$-differential is induced by $f$ on the $E_\infty$-pages.
  
  Differentials in this spectral sequence has the form
  $$d_n^{f}: \ESS{f}_n^{s,t}\to \ESS{f}_n^{s+n, t+n}.$$

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapExtension.differentialRelation_iff
lean.code:
public theorem differentialRelation_iff (f : FilteredMorphism F G)
    (hF : F.IsBounded) (hG : G.IsBounded) (k : ω) (s : ℤ) (n : ℕ)
    {T : C} [Projective T] (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded s k)
    (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded (s + (n : ℤ)) k) :
    DifferentialRelation (sequence f hF hG k) n (s, 1)
      (x ≫ (sourceIso f hF hG k s).inv)
      (y ≫ (targetIso f hF hG k s n).inv) ↔ Relation f k s n x y := by
  rw [relation_iff_fiber, and_iff_right (Int.natCast_nonneg n)]
  change DifferentialRelation
    ((underlyingComplex f.map f.compat k).toSpectralSequence
      (underlyingComplexBounded f.map f.compat k hF hG)) n (s, 1)
    (x ≫ 𝟙 (F.associatedGraded s k)) (y ≫ 𝟙 (G.associatedGraded (s + ↑n) k)) ↔ _
  rw [Category.comp_id, Category.comp_id]
  exact
    FilteredComplex.Solutions.differentialRelation_iff_nonempty_fiber
      (underlyingComplex f.map f.compat k)
      (underlyingComplexBounded f.map f.compat k hF hG) n s 1 x y
lean.statement:
public theorem differentialRelation_iff (f : FilteredMorphism F G)
    (hF : F.IsBounded) (hG : G.IsBounded) (k : ω) (s : ℤ) (n : ℕ)
    {T : C} [Projective T] (x : T ⟶ F.associatedGraded s k)
    (y : T ⟶ G.associatedGraded (s + (n : ℤ)) k) :
    DifferentialRelation (sequence f hF hG k) n (s, 1)
      (x ≫ (sourceIso f hF hG k s).inv)
      (y ≫ (targetIso f hF hG k s n).inv) ↔ Relation f k s n x y
lean.docstring:
The actual ESS differential relation is precisely the original filtered-map
equation. Projectivity is retained when arbitrary morphism-valued labels are used.

entries.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions
entries.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 2.6.)

If the Adams filtration of $f$ is $k$, then
    $d^f_i=0$ for $i<k$.

comments.author: metadata-migration
comments.title: Module interface conventions
comments.text:
Module-level interface conventions; completion remains derived from verified Lean evidence.

- **principle**: 普通公共导入即可调用同一固定背景上的对象与定理；下游不传入结果包。保留真正数学前提；未完成构造与证明逐项登记，不能把可调用误报为已证明。

- **type_authority**: Complete types and universe/typeclass assumptions live in the referenced Lean declarations. The API manifest and normal-import tests freeze their elaborated types; this semantic ledger is not a second Lean source registry.

- **exclusions**: README and AGENTS edits

- **exclusions**: Blueprint migration/checks

- **exclusions**: Literature/Computation/ProofTools/Main implementations

- **exclusions**: raw CSV/Generated/checkers

- **exclusions**: full completion-model identification and derived-source unitor are explicit unfinished source tasks

- **weight_direction_correction.statement**: For w1≤w2≤t, the quotient and actual lambda map lower weight w2→w1.

- **weight_direction_correction.reason**: B_(1+t-w2) ≤ B_(1+t-w1); the old reverse quotient map was not well-defined in general.

- **weight_direction_correction.affected_type**: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.NuInfinityWeightMaps

- **weight_direction_correction.compatibility**: Intentional signature correction; former type freeze updated and tracking retained.

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.statement**: NuExactTriangleInput requires injectivity, middle exactness and surjectivity in every HF2-homology degree.

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.reason**: Middle exactness of a distinguished triangle alone does not imply that nu preserves its cofiber.

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.affected_type**: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.NuExactTriangleInput.preserves

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.compatibility**: Intentional correction of an overly strong legacy input; the same predicate is reused by the full Literature iff.

- **constraints**: PointSet category/model/pointed structures and localization into current C. StableLocalization binds derived suspension to C shift and model cofiber squares to existing distinguished triangles; stable square and comparison conditions are retained. Classical data include closed symmetric point-set tensor, limits/colimits, cofibrant generation with small-object conditions, pushout-product/unit laws, natural tensor comparison on cofibrant inputs and replacement-unit/sphere comparison.

- **constraints**: A global selected model is replaced by an optional supplied realization of the existing C. Ho-equivalence and quotient compatibility are derived from localization; suspension-loop unit/counit invertibility is derived.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:nu-exactness
entries.title: When nu preserves a cofiber triangle
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
Let $X	o Y	o Z	o\Sigma X$ be a distinguished triangle in $\mathrm{Sp}$. If its mod-two homology forms a short exact sequence in every degree, then there exists $h\colon
u Z	o\Sigma
u X$ such that $
u X	o
u Y	o
u Z\xrightarrow{h}\Sigma
u X$ is a distinguished triangle in $\mathrm{Syn}$.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.nu_preserves_triangle
lean.code:
public theorem nu_preserves_triangle (T : CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle Spectrum)
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang Spectrum) (hH : HomologyShortExact coefficients T) :
    ∃ h : nu.functor.obj T.obj₃ ⟶
        (shiftFunctor SyntheticSpectrum (1 : ℤ)).obj (nu.functor.obj T.obj₁),
      CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk
        (nu.functor.map T.mor₁) (nu.functor.map T.mor₂) h ∈ distTriang SyntheticSpectrum := by
  sorry

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:sphere-sign
entries.title: The sign of the sphere twist
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For integers $r,s$, the braiding $S^r\wedge S^s\to S^s\wedge S^r$ is multiplication by $(-1)^{rs}$ under the sphere-smash identifications with $S^{r+s}$ and the identification $r+s=s+r$.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.sphere_twist
lean.code:
public theorem sphere_twist (r s : ℤ) :
    letI := closedBackground.symmetric
    (β_ (Sphere r : Spectrum) (Sphere s)).hom ≫ (closedBackground.smashSpheres s r).hom ≫
      eqToHom (congrArg (Sphere (C := Spectrum)) (add_comm s r)) =
      if Even (r * s) then (closedBackground.smashSpheres r s).hom
      else -(closedBackground.smashSpheres r s).hom := by sorry

public theorem sphere_twist (r s : ℤ) :
    letI

- **constraints**: The spectral ambient is isomorphic to the actual Z2 submodule, and every finite Z/B membership is fixed by the raw tower.

- **constraints**: Differentials use the actual connecting lift and cofiber image, including zero representatives.

- **constraints**: Classical naturality compares the same family morphism to the selected stage/cofiber map; synthetic natural_e2 allows their raw representatives to differ by an actual B2 boundary, retaining the original quotient-level law.

entries.title: The classical page and differential conventions
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, the Adams spectral sequence begins at $E_2$ and its page-$r$ differential has degree $(r,r-1)$. For $f\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to Z$, one has $E(g\circ f)=E(g)\circ E(f)$.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:filtration-comparison
entries.title: Two descriptions of Adams filtration
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Let $f$ be a map in $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $s\in\mathbb Z$. The map $f$ has filtration at least $s$ with respect to the Adams tower of its target if and only if it has filtration at least $s$ defined by factorization into maps inducing zero in mod-two homology.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:finite-separation
entries.title: Separation for maps of finite spectra
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a map between finite spectra. If $f$ lies in every integer stage of the Adams filtration, then $f$ is odd torsion. The same assertion holds for the factorization filtration. Consequently, every map between finite spectra which is not odd torsion has an exact finite integer filtration.

  KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.finite_filtration_of_not_odd classicalTower
    finite_map_separation hX hY f hf

entries.title: Bounded filtration in a fixed homotopy degree
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Let $X$ be finite, rationally acyclic, and homotopy two-local. For every $i\in\mathbb Z$, there is an integer $N$ such that $F^s\pi_i(X)=0$ for all $s\geq N$, where $F$ is the coefficient-tower Adams filtration.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:classical-vanishing
entries.title: Low-filtration support and sphere separation
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, one has $E_r^{s,t}(X)=0$ whenever $s<0$. For the sphere, $E_r^{0,t}(S)=0$ for every nonzero $t\geq0$. A sphere homotopy class lying in $F^s$ for every $s\in\mathbb N$ is odd torsion.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.sphere_page_filtration_zero
lean.code:
public theorem sphere_page_filtration_zero (r : ℤ) (t : ℕ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    Subsingleton (model.classical.sphere.Page r (0,t)) := by
  let T := model.classicalTower.tower (SphereSpectrum (C := Spectrum))
  let e : T.layer 0 ≅ model.coefficients.object :=
    T.layerIso 0 ≪≫ (tensorLeft model.coefficients.object).mapIso T.zeroIso ≪≫
      ρ_ model.coefficients.object
  letI := model.coefficients.homotopy_vanishes (t : ℤ) (by exact_mod_cast ht)
  letI : Subsingleton (T.FirstPage (0,t)) := by
    change Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup (t : ℤ) (T.layer 0))
    exact (Iso.homCongr (Iso.refl (Sphere (C := Spectrum) (t : ℤ))) e).injective.subsingleton
  let D := model.classical.sphere.ssData (0,t)
  letI : Subsingleton D.V :=
    (model.classicalTower.sequence (SphereSpectrum (C := Spectrum))).ambient (0,t)
      |>.toLinearEquiv.injective.subsingleton
  exact page_subsingleton_of_ambient D _

public theorem classical_page_negative (X : ClassicalObject) (r s t : ℤ)
    (hs : s < 0) :
    Subsingleton ((model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).Page r (s,t)) := by
  let T := model.classicalTower.tower (X.obj model.auxiliary)
  have hi (a b : ℕ) (hab : a ≤ b) (h : a = b) : IsIso (T.map hab) := by
    subst b
    rw [T.map_self]
    infer_instance
  let f := T.mapAt (show s ≤ s+1 by omega)
  haveI : IsIso f := hi s.toNat (s+1).toNat (by omega) (by omega)
  have hLayer : IsZero (T.layer s) :=
    Pretriangulated.Triangle.isZero₃_of_isIso₁
      (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk f (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibι f)
        (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibδ f))
      (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofib_distinguished f) (show IsIso f from inferInstance)
  letI : Subsingleton (T.FirstPage (s,t)) := ⟨fun a b => hLayer.eq_of_tgt a b⟩
  let D := (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).ssData (s,t)
  letI : Subsingleton D.V :=
    (model.classicalTower.sequence (X.obj model.auxiliary)).ambient (s,t)
      |>.toLinearEquiv.injective.subsingleton
  exact page_subsingleton_of_ambient D _

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:homology-exact
entries.title: Cofiber homology and a cardinality bound
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Mod-two homology of a cofiber sequence is exact at the cofiber term, with boundary induced by the cofiber map to the suspension. Suppose that every finite subset of the two adjacent homology groups has cardinality at most $n_X$ and $n_Y$, respectively. Then every finite subset of the cofiber homology group has cardinality at most $n_Xn_Y$.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.homology_exact
lean.code:
public theorem homology_exact (T : HoCofiberSequence (C := Spectrum)) (i : ℤ) :
    Function.Exact (modTwoHomologyMap coefficients T.g i)
      (modTwoConnecting coefficients homologyShift T i) := by
  let U := Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk (coefficients.object ◁ T.f)
    (coefficients.object ◁ T.g) (coefficients.object ◁ T.h ≫ (homologyShift T.X).hom)
  have hU : U ∈ distTriang Spectrum := homology_triangle_distinguished T
  intro z
  change AbstractAdamsTower.desuspend (coefficients.object ⊗ T.X) i
    (z ≫ U.mor₃) = 0 ↔ ∃ y, y ≫ U.mor₂ = z
  have hzero : AbstractAdamsTower.desuspend (coefficients.object ⊗ T.X) i
      (z ≫ U.mor₃) = 0 ↔ z ≫ U.mor₃ = 0 := by
    constructor
    · intro hz
      apply desuspend_injective (coefficients.object ⊗ T.X) i
      simpa only [map_zero] using hz
    · intro hz
      rw [hz, map_zero]
  rw [hzero]
  constructor
  · intro hz
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := Pretriangulated.Triangle.coyoneda_exact₃ U hU z hz
    exact ⟨y, hy.symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
    rw [Category.assoc, Pretriangulated.comp_distTriang_mor_zero₂₃ U hU, comp_zero]

entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

comments.author: metadata-migration
comments.title: Interface scope: synthetic-homotopy-separation
comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `synthetic-homotopy-separation`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: 同一固定 synthetic 塔在所选对象实际有限 λⁿ 商上的同伦滤过分离性；不再断言未截断普通球/ν 对象的全称零结论。

- **scope**: XModLambdaN (X.obj model.nu model.auxiliary) n for X : SyntheticObject and n : ℕ; the same actual lambda cofiber and synthetic tower

- **not_asserted**: Separation for every object of SyntheticSpectrum

- **not_asserted**: A uniform or finite filtration bound

- **not_asserted**: Classical finite-map odd-torsion separation

- **not_asserted**: An automatic consequence of canonical E-infinity identification

- **not_asserted**: Untruncated sphere or arbitrary nu-object Hausdorffness

- **not_asserted**: Vanishing of odd-primary infinite-filtration classes on the ordinary sphere


Code provenance: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSource871b3be8f46a](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/871b3be8f46a1c02d49011e9c6495ec3d938b338), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:canonical-tower
entries.title: The canonical coefficient-unit Adams tower
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, define its canonical Adams tower recursively by taking fibers of the coefficient-unit maps. Its spectral sequence has the tower cycles and boundaries as cycle and boundary subgroups, with limiting cycles given by their intersection and limiting boundaries by their union.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:canonical-comparison
entries.title: Comparison with the canonical tower sequence
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For every $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, its classical Adams sequence is isomorphic to the canonical coefficient-tower sequence. This isomorphism identifies ambient groups, finite pages, differentials, infinite cycles, and infinite boundaries. For sphere classes it preserves and reflects nonzero permanent survival.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.nonzeroSurvival_source_iff
lean.code:
public theorem nonzeroSurvival_source_iff (p : ℤ × ℤ) (x : classical.sphere.Page 2 p) :
    NonzeroSurvival canonicalSphereSequence p
      (classicalSphere_sourceIso.hom.pageMap 2 p x) ↔
        NonzeroSurvival classical.sphere p x :=
  Internal.Source.nonzeroSurvival_iso_iff classicalSphere_sourceIso p x
lean.statement:

    NonzeroSurvival canonicalSphereSequence p
      (classicalSphere_sourceIso.hom.pageMap 2 p x) ↔
        NonzeroSurvival classical.sphere p x
lean.docstring:
Permanent nonzero survival transports with the same infinite
representative, rather than merely a vector-space isomorphism on E₂.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:hf2-localization
entries.title: The mod-two-localized classical sequence
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: The classical Adams functor sends mod-two homology equivalences to isomorphisms and hence factors through localization at these equivalences. The resulting localized sphere sequence is isomorphic to the ordinary classical sphere sequence; let the localized $h_6^2$ be the class corresponding to $h_6^2$ under this isomorphism.

public theorem standardH6Square_milnor :
    sphereE2_milnorEquiv 2 128 standardH6Square = milnorHiSquareClass 6 := by
  have h := sphereProduct_milnor 1 64 1 64 standardH6 standardH6
  simp only [standardH6Square_eq_product] at ⊢
  change sphereE2_milnorEquiv 2 128
    (sphereAlgebra.product (1,64) (1,64) standardH6 standardH6) = _
  change sphereE2_milnorEquiv 2 128
    (sphereAlgebra.product (1,64) (1,64) standardH6 standardH6) = _ at h
  rw [h]
  have hh : sphereE2_milnorEquiv 1 64 standardH6 = milnorHiClass 6 :=
    standardHi_milnor 6
  rw [hh]
  exact (Milnor.hiSquare_eq_cup 6).symm

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-detection
entries.title: Detection of maps in the mapping spectral sequence
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For finite spectra $X,Y$, the Adams filtration of $f\colon X\to Y$ equals that of its class in $\pi_0F(X,Y)$. Exact filtration is detected by the convergence quotient comparison. If $f$ is not odd torsion, it has a nonzero $E_\infty$ detector represented by a common infinite cycle.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-laws
entries.title: Associativity and units for mapping composition
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: The finite-page mapping pairings are associative under the degree identifications and have compatible left and right units. Each unit is represented by a common infinite cycle whose abutment is the identity map.

comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `standard-sphere-classes`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: 同一实际球谱E₂的F₂乘法及指定标准h_i，平方使用该乘法。

- **constraints**: The existing standardHi construction is retained. Its separately registered identity theorem fixes it to the specified ξ₁^(2^i) class through the same actual E₁/d₁/E₂ descent diagram.

- **constraints**: The E₂ comparison must descend the actual tower coordinates, rather than be an unrelated graded linear equivalence.

- **constraints**: The actual sphere product and unit must agree with the independently defined cobar cup product and unit.

- **constraints**: No uniqueness or nonvanishing of the entire h_i family is assumed; h6-square nonvanishing is separate.

- **constraints**: No permanent-survival conclusion is an AdamsSynthetic input.

- **roles**: data

- **roles**: operation

- **roles**: structural-law

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:enriched-composition
entries.title: Enriched composition agrees on all three layers
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: On elementary products, enriched composition agrees with the mapping composition pairing on every finite page, on $E_\infty$, and on the abutment. The enriched identities agree with the mapping units on each of these three levels.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.mappingEnriched_composition_abutment
lean.code:
public theorem mappingEnriched_composition_abutment : letI := mappingEnriched_monoidal
    ∀ (X Y Z : MappingObject (IsFiniteSpectrum (C := Spectrum))) (i j : ℤ)
      (x : (mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.A i) (y : (mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.A j),
      let f : (mappingSystem.hom X Y ⊗ mappingSystem.hom Y Z) ⟶ mappingSystem.hom X Z :=
        eqToHom (congrArg₂ (fun A B : ConvergingSequence.{0,0} ℤ => A ⊗ B)
          (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Y).symm (mappingEnriched_hom_eq Y Z).symm) ≫ mappingEnriched_enriched.comp X Y Z ≫
            eqToHom (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Z)
      f.convergence.aMap (i+j) ((mappingEnriched_tensorPairing X Y Z).abutmentPair i j x y) =
        (mappingComposition.pairing X Y Z).abutmentPair i j x y := by sorry

lean.code:
public theorem mappingEnriched_composition_eInfty : letI := mappingEnriched_monoidal
    ∀ (X Y Z : MappingObject (IsFiniteSpectrum (C := Spectrum))) (i j : ℤ × ℤ)
      (x : ((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).eInfty)
      (y : ((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).eInfty),
      let f : (mappingSystem.hom X Y ⊗ mappingSystem.hom Y Z) ⟶ mappingSystem.hom X Z :=
        eqToHom (congrArg₂ (fun A B : ConvergingSequence.{0,0} ℤ => A ⊗ B)
          (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Y).symm (mappingEnriched_hom_eq Y Z).symm) ≫ mappingEnriched_enriched.comp X Y Z ≫
            eqToHom (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Z)
      f.sequence.eInftyMap (i+j) ((mappingEnriched_tensorPairing X Y Z).eInftyPair i j x y) =
        (mappingComposition.pairing X Y Z).eInftyPair i j x y := by
  letI := mappingEnriched_monoidal
  intro X Y Z i j x y
  let f : (mappingSystem.hom X Y ⊗ mappingSystem.hom Y Z) ⟶ mappingSystem.hom X Z :=
    eqToHom (congrArg₂ (fun A B : ConvergingSequence.{0,0} ℤ => A ⊗ B)
      (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Y).symm (mappingEnriched_hom_eq Y Z).symm) ≫
        mappingEnriched_enriched.comp X Y Z ≫ eqToHom (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Z)
  let P := mappingEnriched_tensorPairing X Y Z
  let Q := mappingComposition.pairing X Y Z
  haveI : Epi (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Epi (cokernel.π _))
  haveI : Epi (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Epi (cokernel.π _))
  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective
    (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤)).mp inferInstance x
  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective
    (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤)).mp inferInstance y
  have h₀ (U V : MappingObject (IsFiniteSpectrum (C := Spectrum))) :
      (mappingSystem.hom U V).underlying.E.r₀ ≤ 2 :=
    le_of_eq (classical.firstPage _)
  have hT : (mappingSystem.hom X Y ⊗ mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.r₀ ≤ 2 :=
    f.sequence.r₀_eq.le.trans (h₀ X Z)
  have h := mappingEnriched_composition_page X Y Z 2 i j
    (infinityToPage _ 2 i a) (infinityToPage _ 2 j b)
  change f.sequence.pageMap 2 (i+j)
      (P.ssPairing.pair 2 i j (infinityToPage _ 2 i a) (infinityToPage _ 2 j b)) =
    Q.ssPairing.pair 2 i j (infinityToPage _ 2 i a) (infinityToPage _ 2 j b) at h
  rw [P.finitePagePair_compatible 2 i j (h₀ X Y) (h₀ Y Z) hT,
    infinityToPage_naturality,
    Q.finitePagePair_compatible 2 i j (h₀ X Y) (h₀ Y Z) (h₀ X Z)] at h
  have hinf := ((mappingSystem.hom X Z).underlying.E.ssData (i+j)).infinity_projection_eq_of_page_projection_eq
    ↑(2 - (mappingSystem.hom X Z).underlying.E.r₀).toNat
    (f.sequence.toSSDataMorphism.cycleMap (i+j) ⊤ (P.cyclePairAtInfinity i j a b))
    (Q.cyclePairAtInfinity i j a b) h
  have htop := congrArg (fun m => m (P.cyclePairAtInfinity i j a b))
    (f.sequence.toSSDataMorphism.pageπ_pageMap (i+j) ⊤)
  change f.sequence.eInftyMap (i+j)
      (P.eInftyPair i j (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤ a)
        (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤ b)) =
    Q.eInftyPair i j (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤ a)
      (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤ b)
  rw [← P.eInftyPair_induced, ← Q.eInftyPair_induced]
  exact htop.trans hinf

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:graded-hom
entries.title: Weight-graded synthetic hom groups
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For synthetic spectra $X,Y$, put $\operatorname{Hom}_w(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Sigma^{0,w}X,Y)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_*(X,Y)=\bigoplus_w\operatorname{Hom}_w(X,Y)$. The total hom group is a $\mathbb Z[\lambda]$-module; multiplication by $\lambda$ lowers weight by one through the shift comparison.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.graded_lambda_smul
lean.code:
public theorem graded_lambda_smul : ∀ (X Y : SyntheticSpectrum) (w : ℤ) (f : WeightHom X Y w),
    letI := graded_module X Y
    (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • weightHomInclusion w f =
      weightHomInclusion (w-1) (weightHomLambda f) := by
  intro X Y w f
  letI := graded_module X Y
  change (Polynomial.eval₂ (Int.castRingHom _) (totalLambda X Y) Polynomial.X) _ = _
  rw [Polynomial.eval₂_X]
  exact totalLambda_of X Y w f

@[implicit_reducible] public def graded_module : ∀ X Y : SyntheticSpectrum, Module (Polynomial ℤ) (TotalWeightHom X Y) := by
  intro X Y
  exact
    (fun (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] (D : M →+ M) =>
      let A := Module.End ℤ M
      letI : Ring A := inferInstance
      let ring : NonAssocRing A := inferInstance
      letI : Module A M := inferInstance
      let L : A := D.toIntLinearMap
      let hom : Polynomial ℤ →+* A :=
        Polynomial.eval₂RingHom' (Int.castRingHom A) L
          (fun a => @Int.cast_commute A ring a L)
      Module.compHom M hom)
      (TotalWeightHom X Y)
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid fun w =>
        (weightHomInclusion (w-1)).comp
          (Preadditive.leftComp Y
            (weightHomLambda (X := X) (𝟙 ((SyntheticCategory.biShift (0,w)).obj X)))))

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:graded-composition
entries.title: Composition in the weight-graded enrichment
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Composition on the weight-graded hom groups is $\mathbb Z[\lambda]$-bilinear. On homogeneous summands it is shifted composition. Under the coherent shift identifications, it is associative and the identity maps are left and right units.

lean.code:
@[no_expose] public def graded_compose : ∀ X Y Z : SyntheticSpectrum,
    letI := graded_module X Y
    letI := graded_module Y Z
    letI := graded_module X Z
    TotalWeightHom Y Z →ₗ[Polynomial ℤ]
      TotalWeightHom X Y →ₗ[Polynomial ℤ] TotalWeightHom X Z := by
  intro X Y Z
  letI := graded_module X Y
  letI := graded_module Y Z
  letI := graded_module X Z
  let C : TotalWeightHom Y Z →+ (TotalWeightHom X Y →+ TotalWeightHom X Z) :=
    totalComp X Y Z
  let F : TotalWeightHom Y Z →+ (TotalWeightHom X Y →ₗ[Polynomial ℤ] TotalWeightHom X Z) :=
    { toFun := fun g =>
        { toFun := C g
          map_add' := (C g).map_add
          map_smul' := by
            intro p f
            apply additive_polynomial_smul (C g) (fun f => ?_) p f
            change totalComp X Y Z g ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • f) =
              (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • totalComp X Y Z g f
            rw [graded_X_smul, graded_X_smul]
            exact totalComp_lambda_right X Y Z f g }
      map_zero' := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro f
        exact congrArg (fun h : TotalWeightHom X Y →+ TotalWeightHom X Z => h f) (map_zero (totalComp X Y Z))
      map_add' := by
        intro g g'
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro f
        exact congrArg (fun h : TotalWeightHom X Y →+ TotalWeightHom X Z => h f) ((totalComp X Y Z).map_add g g') }
  exact
    { toFun := F
      map_add' := F.map_add
      map_smul' := by
        intro p g
        apply additive_polynomial_smul F (fun g => ?_) p g
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro f
        change totalComp X Y Z ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • g) f =
          (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • totalComp X Y Z g f
        rw [graded_X_smul, graded_X_smul]
        exact totalComp_lambda_left X Y Z f g }

comments.title: Interface scope: obligation-zlambda-enrichment
comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `obligation-zlambda-enrichment`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: Hom 分量就是 Hom(Σ^(0,w) X,Y)，总 Hom 是这些实际 Hom 的直和；不是任意新选对象。 Polynomial.X 在直和注入上等于由同一 lam 和同一 shift comparison 构成的 weightHomLambda；权重降低一。 复合是 ℤ[λ] 双线性，齐次分量上的复合等于实际移位映射复合；单位由同一 biShift_zero 得到。 修正旧未分次 EnrichedCategory(ModuleCat ℤ[λ]) 的语义：普通 Syn 是分次富集的零次部分；不宣称 λ 是固定权重 Hom 上的自映射。 结合律和左右单位律从同一 shift coherence、齐次实际复合相容式及 DirectSum 加法归纳推导，已经删除重复输入字段。

- **constraints**: Hom 分量就是 Hom(Σ^(0,w) X,Y)，总 Hom 是这些实际 Hom 的直和；不是任意新选对象。 Polynomial.X 在直和注入上等于由同一 lam 和同一 shift comparison 构成的 weightHomLambda；权重降低一。 复合是 ℤ[λ] 双线性，齐次分量上的复合等于实际移位映射复合；单位由同一 biShift_zero 得到。 修正旧未分次 EnrichedCategory(ModuleCat ℤ[λ]) 的语义：普通 Syn 是分次富集的零次部分；不宣称 λ 是固定权重 Hom 上的自映射。 结合律和左右单位律从同一 shift coherence、齐次实际复合相容式及 DirectSum 加法归纳推导，已经删除重复输入字段。

- **constraints**: 旧未分次富集声明没有绑定权重；新合同在 ⨁ w, Hom(Σ^(0,w) X,Y) 上交付 ℤ[λ] 富集，并将普通 Syn 解释为零次部分。λ 降权一，不能在固定权重 Hom 内强行当作自映射。

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:e2-comparison
entries.title: The classical-to-synthetic second-page comparison
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: The classical-to-synthetic comparison identifies classical $E_2$ classes with synthetic $E_2$ classes at the corresponding weights. The image of the corresponding synthetic $E_2$ label under the quotient page map detects the first $\lambda$-quotient homotopy class. For the sphere, this identification is compatible with the quotient map and powers of $\lambda$ through their detection identities.

lean.code:
public theorem sphere_first_quotient : ∀ (s t : ℤ) (x : classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t)),
    Detects (convergence (.quotient 1 .sphere)) (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl S_0_0 1) 2 (s,t,t)
        (by simpa only [SyntheticAdamsFamily.sphere, SyntheticAdamsSS.Page,
          Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x))
      ((sphereFirstQuotient nu quotients.functoriality firstQuotient s t).symm x) := by
  intro s t x
  let Z := (SyntheticCategory.biShift (0,0)).obj (nu.functor.obj SphereSpectrum)
  let e : Z ≅ (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) :=
    SyntheticCategory.biShift_zero.app _ ≪≫ nu.unitIso
  let q := (quotients.functoriality.functor 1).mapIso e
  let u0 : (family.obj Z).Page 2 (s,t,t+0) := by
    simpa only [Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero, ClassicalObject.obj] using
      comparison.nuE2 .sphere 0 s t 0 x
  let u := trPage (Int.add_zero t) u0
  let b0 := (firstQuotient .sphere 0 s t).symm x
  let b := trHom (Int.add_zero t) b0
  have hd0 := first_quotient .sphere 0 s t x
  have hd : KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Detects
      (convergence (.quotient 1 (.shift (0,0) (.nu .sphere)))) (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) 2 (s,t,t) u) b := by
    have ht := detects_tr _ (Int.add_zero t) hd0
    have htr := pageMap_tr family (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) (Int.add_zero t) u0
    exact htr ▸ ht
  let M := Classical.choice (canonical_convergence_natural syntheticTower q.hom
    (convergence (.quotient 1 (.shift (0,0) (.nu .sphere))))
    (convergence (.quotient 1 .sphere)))
  have hm := detects_map M (s,t,t) hd
  have hn : family.pageMap e.hom 2 (s,t,t) u =
      (by simpa only [SyntheticAdamsFamily.sphere, SyntheticAdamsSS.Page,
        Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x) := by
    let un0 : (family.obj Z).Page 2 (s,t,t-(0 : ℕ)) := by
      simpa only [add_zero, ClassicalObject.obj] using comparison.nuE2 .sphere 0 s t 0 x
    have h0 := comparison.sphere_nu s t 0 x
    change family.pageMap e.hom 2 (s,t,t-(0 : ℕ)) un0 = comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x at h0
    have ht := congrArg (trPage (F := family) (X := (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum))
      (s := s) (t := t) (show t-(0 : ℕ) = t by simp)) h0
    have htr := pageMap_tr family e.hom (show t-(0 : ℕ) = t by simp) un0
    rw [htr] at ht
    simpa only [u, u0, un0, trPage, eq_mp_eq_cast, cast_cast, id_eq] using ht
  have hp : family.pageMap q.hom 2 (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) 2 (s,t,t) u) =
      family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl S_0_0 1) 2 (s,t,t)
        (by simpa only [SyntheticAdamsFamily.sphere, SyntheticAdamsSS.Page,
          Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x) := by
    change (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) 2 (s,t,t) ≫
      family.pageMap q.hom 2 (s,t,t)) u = _
    rw [← familyPageMap_comp]
    change family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1 ≫ XModLambdaN.map e.hom 1) 2 (s,t,t) u = _
    rw [← XModLambdaN.incl_naturality, familyPageMap_comp]
    change family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl S_0_0 1) 2 (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap e.hom 2 (s,t,t) u) = _
    rw [hn]
  have hb : b ≫ q.hom = (sphereFirstQuotient nu quotients.functoriality firstQuotient s t).symm x := by
    have hcast := linearEquiv_cast_symm
      (A := fun w => BiHom (t-s) w (XModLambdaN Z 1))
      (Int.add_zero t) (firstQuotient .sphere 0 s t) x

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:normalized-map
entries.title: Normalized synthetic maps
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: For a map $f$ between objects of $\mathcal C_0$, its normalized synthetic lift is obtained from $\nu(f)$ with exponent determined by whether $f$ factors through the first stage of the target Adams tower. Composing this lift with the corresponding power of $\lambda$ gives $\nu(f)$. Every map between objects of $\mathcal S_0$ induces a morphism of converging Adams sequences.

comments.title: Interface scope: normalized-extension-language
comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `normalized-extension-language`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: 同一actual map的归一化lift及有限/无限延拓见证；未输入传播定理。

- **constraints**: ExtensionEquation is the actual two-term filtered-map solution fiber.

- **constraints**: The full target coset uses the actual shorter-extension boundary subobject, not a selected finite subset.

- **constraints**: Length-zero extension must be derived from the same actual map on E-infinity and canonical convergence naturality.

- **constraints**: Finite witnesses retain page>=2, lower/upper length bounds, source/target cycle levels and common infinity representatives.

- **constraints**: Infinite witnesses retain common permanent representatives and the normalized lower length bound.

- **constraints**: Bounded ESS hypotheses remain separate from general unbounded extension equations.

- **roles**: data

- **roles**: predicate

- **roles**: derived-theorem

- **mathematical_review.finite_cycle_translation**: IsCycle(level) is translated to ReachesPage(level+1). Thus source page r and target page r-n+e retain the old r-1 and r-1-n+e cycle levels. Target page >=2 follows from length_upper.

- **mathematical_review.permanent_translation**: Old permanentCycles is the range of the common Z-infinity representative into E2; IsPermanentCycle preserves that semantics including zero.

- **mathematical_review.normalization**: e(f)=1 iff the same actual target tower admits a stage-one factorization, otherwise zero; no independently supplied filtration integer.

- **mathematical_review.homology_exactness**: NuExactTriangleInput uses the actual inducedMap (H.object whiskerLeft f); complete injective/exact/surjective conditions correct the old middle-only premise.

entries.title: Functoriality and naturality of weight maps
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Weight-lowering maps are identities at equal weights and compose along ordered weights. For $w_1\leq w_2\leq t$, they commute with the $E_\infty$ maps induced by $\nu(f)$.

entries.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:shift-representatives
entries.title: Shift transport of common representatives
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Let $r\geq2$ be a finite page. Under the synthetic shift comparison, two shifted classes have a common representative if and only if the corresponding unshifted classes do, using the induced filtered map on homotopy groups.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.shift_representative_iff
lean.code:
public theorem shift_representative_iff (δ : ℤ × ℤ) : ∀ (X : SyntheticObject) (r : ℤ) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
      (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s : ℤ)
      (x : (model.family.obj (X.obj model.nu model.auxiliary)).Page r (s,p.1+s,p.2))
      (z : ((model.family.obj (X.obj model.nu model.auxiliary)).sequence.ssData (s,p.1+s,p.2)).eInfty),
    HasInfinityRepresentative _ r (s,p.1+s,p.2) x z ↔
      HasInfinityRepresentative _ r (s,(p+δ).1+s,(p+δ).2)
        (((shift_page δ) X r hr p s).hom x)
        ((towerInfinityIso (model.convergence X) (model.convergence (.shift δ X))
          ((shift_filtered δ) X p) s).hom z) := by sorry

entries.label: paper:3.3
entries.title: The class $\lambda$ and its cofibers
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 3.3.)

[{\cite{Pst} ([Definition 4.27])}]
    The natural comparison map
    $$S^{0,-1}=\Sus \nu (S^{-1})\to \nu(\Sus S^{-1})=S^{0,0}$$
    in the category of $\HF$-synthetic spectra is denoted by $\lambda\in \pi_{0,-1}S^{0,0}$. We denote by $S^{0,0}/\lambda$ the cofiber of $\lambda$. In general for synthetic $X$ the following
    $$\lambda\wedge id_X: \Sus^{0,-1}X\to X.$$
    is a natural transformation and by abuse of notation this map is also denoted by $\lambda$.
    We denote by $X/\lambda$ the cofiber of $\lambda$
    which is equivalent to $(S^{0,0}/\lambda) \wedge X$.

lean.name: KIP126.Synthetic.Context.SyntheticCategory
lean.code:
public class SyntheticCategory (Syn : Type u) extends
    StableHomotopyCategory.{u, v} Syn where
  biShift : ℤ × ℤ → Syn ⥤ Syn
  biShift_comp : ∀ (a b : ℤ × ℤ),
    biShift a ⋙ biShift b ≅ biShift (a + b)
  biShift_zero : biShift (0, 0) ≅ 𝟭 Syn
  biShift_compat : ∀ n : ℤ, biShift (n, 0) ≅ shiftFunctor Syn n
  /-- Each bigraded suspension is fully faithful (the inverse suspension is
      supplied by the same coherence data in a concrete model). -/
  biShift_fullyFaithful : ∀ p : ℤ × ℤ, (biShift p).FullyFaithful
  lam : biShift (0, -1) ⟶ 𝟭 Syn
  biShift_tensor_comm : ∀ (p : ℤ × ℤ) (X Y : Syn),
    (biShift p).obj (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj X Y) ≅
      MonoidalCategory.tensorObj ((biShift p).obj X) Y

A stable category with a coherent bigraded suspension and deformation map.

The parent class supplies the additive, shifted, monoidal, and triangulated
structure.  `biShift` records the extra synthetic grading, while `lam` is the
natural transformation
`Σ^(0,-1) ⟶ Id` used to define the λ-power quotients.

lean.name: KIP126.Synthetic.Context.lambdaPow
lean.code:
public noncomputable def lambdaPow : (n : ℕ) → (X : Syn) →
    (SyntheticCategory.biShift (0, -(n : ℤ))).obj X ⟶ X
  | 0, X => SyntheticCategory.biShift_zero.hom.app X
  | n + 1, X => by
      have step1 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -1) ⋙
            SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).map
            (SyntheticCategory.lam.app X) ≫ lambdaPow n X
      have step2 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0, -1) + (0, -(n : ℤ)))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift_comp (0, -1) (0, -(n : ℤ))).inv.app X ≫ step1
      have heq :
          ((0 : ℤ), (-1 : ℤ)) + ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ)) =
            ((0 : ℤ), -(↑(n + 1) : ℤ)) := by
        simp
      exact heq ▸ step2
lean.statement:
public noncomputable def lambdaPow : (n : ℕ) → (X : Syn) →
    (SyntheticCategory.biShift (0, -(n : ℤ))).obj X ⟶ X
  | 0, X => SyntheticCategory.biShift_zero.hom.app X
  | n + 1, X => by
      have step1 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -1) ⋙
            SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).map
            (SyntheticCategory.lam.app X) ≫ lambdaPow n X
      have step2 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0, -1) + (0, -(n : ℤ)))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift_comp (0, -1) (0, -(n : ℤ))).inv.app X ≫ step1
      have heq :
          ((0 : ℤ), (-1 : ℤ)) + ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ)) =
            ((0 : ℤ), -(↑(n + 1) : ℤ)) := by
        simp
      exact heq ▸ step2
lean.docstring:
The `n`-fold composite of the deformation map `λ` on `X`.

The recursive definition follows the coherence isomorphism supplied by
`biShift_comp`; in particular `lambdaPow 0 X` is the chosen identity
isomorphism from `Σ^(0,0)X` to `X`.

entries.label: paper:2.3
entries.title: Extensions and essential extensions
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 2.3.)


    We say there is an $f$-extension from $x\in E_\infty^{s,t}(X)$ to $y\in E_\infty^{s+n,t+n}(Y)$ if $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ in the $f$-ESS. We say this $f$-extension is $\textbf{essential}$ if $y$ is nontrivial in the $E_n$-page of the $f$-ESS, or equivalently $$y\notin \BESS{f}^{s+n,t+n}_{n-1}(Y).$$
    Otherwise we refer to it as inessential.

public theorem mem_indeterminacy_iff :
    z ∈ TargetIndeterminacy f k s n T ↔
      0 ≤ n ∧ ∃ (a : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (F.F (s + 1) k))
        (b : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (G.F (s + n) k)),
        b ≫ G.toAssociatedGraded (s + n) k = z ∧
        a ≫ (F.F (s + 1) k).arrow ≫ f.map k =
          b ≫ (G.F (s + n) k).arrow := by
  let i := Subobject.ofLE (F.F (s + 1) k) (F.F s k) (F.mono s k)
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hn, a, b, ha, hb, he⟩
    have ha0 : a ≫ cokernel.π i = 0 := ha
    let a' := Abelian.monoLift i a ha0
    have ha' : a' ≫ i = a := Abelian.monoLift_comp i a ha0
    refine ⟨hn, a', b, hb, ?_⟩
    rw [← ha'] at he
    simpa only [Category.assoc, i, Subobject.ofLE_arrow_assoc] using he

    · change (a ≫ i) ≫ cokernel.π i = 0
      rw [Category.assoc, cokernel.condition, comp_zero]
    · simpa only [Category.assoc, i, Subobject.ofLE_arrow_assoc] using he

entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, $a,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, and $k\in\mathbb N$, there are linear isomorphisms
\[
K_{X,a,k}\colon E_2^{s,t}(X)\cong E_2^{s,t,t+a-k}(\Sigma^{0,a}\nu X),\qquad
K_{S,k}\colon E_2^{s,t}(S)\cong E_2^{s,t,t-k}(S^{0,0}).
\]
They commute with maps between objects of $\mathcal C_0$. The sphere comparison agrees with the $X=S$, $a=0$ comparison under $\nu S\cong S^{0,0}$, and the map induced by $\lambda$ sends $K_{X,-1,k}(x)$ to $K_{X,0,k+1}(x)$.

entries.title: Classical convergence and suspension
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, the classical Adams sequence has canonical isomorphisms
\[
E_\infty^{s,t}(X)\cong\operatorname{gr}_F^s\pi_{t-s}X.
\]
The isomorphisms identify the class of an infinite cycle represented by a tower lift with the associated graded class of the projection of that same lift. The tower of $\Sigma X$ is isomorphic stagewise and layerwise to the suspension of the tower of $X$. These isomorphisms commute with tower maps, the stage-zero comparison, and layer inclusions; the layer connecting maps commute with a minus sign under the suspension-interchange comparison.

entries.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:5934d2f3caff
entries.title: Point-set realizations, cofibers, and smash products
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
The classical and synthetic categories have stable point-set model realizations whose homotopy categories are equivalent to $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $\mathrm{Syn}$, respectively. The classical model is closed symmetric monoidal, complete, cocomplete, and cofibrantly generated; its model tensor is compatible with the model structure. On cofibrant inputs, localization identifies its tensor with the tensor in $\mathrm{Sp}$, naturally in both inputs, and sends a cofibrant replacement of its unit to $S$.

Write $Q$ for passage from classical prespectra to $\mathrm{Sp}$ under the source equivalence. For well-based prespectra $X,Y$ and $f\colon X\to Y$, there is an isomorphism $Q\operatorname{Cone}(f)\cong C(Qf)$ commuting with the cone inclusion and boundary. For good based spaces $A,B$, there is a natural isomorphism $Q\Sigma^\infty A\otimes Q\Sigma^\infty B\cong Q\Sigma^\infty(A\wedge B)$ compatible with the left unit. For all prespectra $X,Y$, the tensor $QX\otimes QY$ is naturally isomorphic to $Q(RX\wedge_{\mathrm{diag}}RY)$, where $R$ is the good replacement functor.

entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: The ordinary stable localization of sequential prespectra is equivalent to $\mathrm{Sp}$. Under this equivalence, the source sphere corresponds to $S$, its identity to the positive sphere generator, and integer stable homotopy groups correspond naturally to the homotopy groups in $\mathrm{Sp}$, preserving zero and stable addition. The equivalence commutes naturally with desuspension and with suspension of well-based prespectra. A source mod-two coefficient prespectrum corresponds to $H\mathbb F_2$, with the same zeroth-homotopy coordinate, vanishing in nonzero degrees, and normalized coefficient unit.

entries.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:b1eb322c2456
entries.title: Associativity and units of mapping pairings
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
For finite spectra $W,X,Y,Z$, page $r\in\mathbb Z$, and page classes $x\in M_r^i(W,X)$, $y\in M_r^j(X,Y)$, and $z\in M_r^k(Y,Z)$, one has
\[
P_r(P_r(x,y),z)=P_r(x,P_r(y,z))
\]
under the identifications of the two degree sums. For finite $X,Y$ and $x\in M_r^k(X,Y)$, the mapping-unit classes satisfy $P_r(u_X,x)=x=P_r(x,u_Y)$ under the zero-degree identifications. The abutment of $u_X$ corresponds to $\operatorname{id}_X\in\pi_0F(X,X)$.

entries.title: Detection, products, and exactness of the synthetic analogue
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, $a,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$, the image of $K_{X,a,0}(x)$ under the first-quotient inclusion detects the inverse image of $x$ in $\pi_{t-s,t+a}((\Sigma^{0,a}\nu X)/\lambda)$.

For a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to\Sigma X$ whose mod-two homology is short exact in every degree, there is a boundary $\nu Z\to\Sigma\nu X$ making the images of its first two maps a distinguished synthetic triangle.

For $s,t\in\mathbb Z$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t}S^{0,0}$, the class $K_{S,k}(q\alpha)$ detects $\lambda^k\alpha$, where $q\alpha$ denotes the classical $E_2$ class obtained from $\alpha$ by the first-quotient comparison.

For $s,t,s',t',k,l\in\mathbb N$, $x\in E_2^{s,t}(S)$, and $y\in E_2^{s',t'}(S)$, if $K_{S,k}(x)$ detects $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t-k}S^{0,0}$ and $K_{S,l}(y)$ detects $\beta\in\pi_{t'-s',t'-l}S^{0,0}$, then $K_{S,k+l}(xy)$ detects $\alpha\beta$ after regrading the degree sums. For $\alpha\in\pi_{m,n}S^{0,0}$ and $\beta\in\pi_{k,l}S^{0,0}$, where $m,n,k,l\in\mathbb Z$, one has $\alpha\beta=(-1)^{mk}\beta\alpha$ after the sum-degree identifications.

entries.title: Enriched composition and identities on pages and abutments
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
Let $X,Y,Z$ be finite spectra, and identify their enriched hom objects with $M(X,Y)$, $M(Y,Z)$, and $M(X,Z)$. Write $c\colon M(X,Y)\otimes M(Y,Z)\to M(X,Z)$ for enriched composition. For $r\in\mathbb Z$, $i,j\in\mathbb Z^2$, and page classes $x,y$ of these degrees,
\[
c_r(T_r(x,y))=P_r(x,y).
\]
For $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and abutment elements $x,y$ of these degrees, one has $c_*(T_*(x,y))=P_*(x,y)$. The enriched identity $e_X\colon\mathbf1\to M(X,X)$ sends the tensor-unit class to the mapping unit on every page $r\in\mathbb Z$ and in the degree-zero abutment.

entries.title: Filtration and normalization identities
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
The following statements hold for the classical coefficient-unit tower and the source comparisons above.
\begin{itemize}
\item For finite $X,Y$, $f\colon X\to Y$, and $s\in\mathbb Z$, $f$ has map Adams filtration at least $s$ if and only if its corresponding class in $\pi_0F(X,Y)$ lies in $F^s$.
\item If $f\colon X\to X'$ and $g\colon Y\to Y'$ are stable equivalences of prespectra, then $Rf\wedge_{\mathrm{diag}}Rg$ is a stable equivalence.
\item For finite, rationally acyclic, homotopy two-local $X$ and $i\in\mathbb Z$, there exists $N\in\mathbb Z$ such that $F^s\pi_iX=0$ whenever $N<s$.
\item For $r,s\in\mathbb Z$, sphere braiding is multiplication by $(-1)^{rs}$ under the sphere-smash comparison with $S^{r+s}$.
\item For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and a first-layer element $z$ of the canonical sphere tower that is a cycle for page two, $\Phi_{s,t}$ sends the class of $z$, transported to the classical sphere sequence, to the Milnor cohomology class of $\phi_{s,t}(z)$.
\item One has $\Phi_{0,0}(1)=1_{\mathrm{Milnor}}$.
\item For $i\in\mathbb N$, one has $\Phi_{1,2^i}(h_i)=h_i^{\mathrm{Milnor}}$.
\end{itemize}

entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
Let $T$ be a coefficient-unit Adams tower, $r\geq2$, and $p=(s,t)\in\mathbb Z^2$. There exists a homomorphism
\[
d_r\colon E_r^p(T)\longrightarrow E_r^{p+(r,r-1)}(T)
\]
with the following representative formula. If $z$ is a cycle representative and its connecting class lifts to $a\in\pi_{t-s-1}T^{s+r}$, then $d_r[z]$ is represented by the layer image of $a$. This formula holds for every such lift and every target cycle representing that layer image.

entries.title: Tower differential identities
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body:
Let $T$ be a coefficient-unit Adams tower and $p\in\mathbb Z^2$. For every integer $r$, one has $d_r^2=0$. For $r\geq2$, with $n=r-2$ and quotient map $q\colon Z_n\to Z_n/B_n$, one has
\[
\ker d_r=\operatorname{im}(Z_{n+1}\longrightarrow Z_n/B_n),\qquad
\operatorname{im}d_r=\operatorname{im}(B_{n+1}\longrightarrow Z_n/B_n).
\]
The kernel formula is in degree $p$, and the image formula is in degree $p+(r,r-1)$.

lean.name: _private.KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Internal.Source.AdamsSequence.0.KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Internal.Source.towerD_image
lean.code:
private theorem towerD_image (T : AbstractAdamsTower unit X) (r : ℤ) (p : ℤ × ℤ)
    (hr : 2 ≤ r) :
    let n := (r - 2).toNat
    let D := towerSSData T (p + (r,r-1))
    imageSubobject (towerD T r p) =
      imageSubobject (Subobject.ofLE (D.B ↑(n + 1)) (D.Z ↑n)
        (le_trans (D.B_le_Z ↑(n + 1))
          (D.Z_anti (by exact_mod_cast Nat.le_succ n))) ≫ D.pageπ ↑n) := by
  sorry

entries.title: Weight maps preserve common representatives
entries.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
entries.body: Let $X\in\mathcal C_0$ and $s,t,w_1,w_2\in\mathbb Z$ with $w_1\leq w_2\leq t$. If $z\in E_\infty^{s,t,w_2}(\nu X)$ and the weight-$w_2$ synthetic label of $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ have a common infinite-cycle representative, then $W_{w_2,w_1}(z)$ and the weight-$w_1$ label of $x$ have a common infinite-cycle representative.

entries.label: sem:Literature:connected-homology
entries.title: Connectivity and mod-two homology
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{SchwedeSymmetricSpectra}, Prop. II.5.22; \cite{EKMM}, Thm. IV.4.5.)\par{}

The sphere is $(-1)$-connected. If $X$ is $n$-connected, then $H_i(X;\mathbb F_2)=0$ for $i\le n$. There is an additive universal-coefficient equivalence
\[H^n(X;\mathbb F_2)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H_{-n}(X;\mathbb F_2),\mathbb F_2).\]
Both groups use the same classical category and coefficient object.

(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.40.)\par{}

Let $\operatorname{Re}$ be the additive realization functor with sphere isomorphisms $S^m\cong\operatorname{Re}(S^{m,w})$. Its isomorphism at the unit is the $\nu$--realization comparison. entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Adams58}, Lem. 2.3; \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.16.)\par{}

The classical maps $\eta$ and $\nu$ are detected by the nonzero permanent cycles $h_1\in E_2^{1,2}$ and $h_2\in E_2^{1,4}$, respectively. The normalized synthetic lift $\eta\in\pi_{1,2}S^{0,0}$ has filtration exponent one, first-quotient label $h_1$, and realization equal to the classical $\eta$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.eta_exponent
lean.code:
public theorem eta_exponent :
  normalizedExponent model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap = 1 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨_, _, b, hb, _⟩ := eta_detection
  have hmem : model.auxiliary.etaMap ∈ ModuleCat.subobjectModule _
      ((model.classicalTower.tower SphereSpectrum).filtration.F 1 1) := by
    change ∃ b, ((model.classicalTower.tower SphereSpectrum).filtration.F 1 1).arrow.hom b = _
    exact ⟨b, hb⟩
  simp only [AbstractAdamsTower.filtration, OrderIso.apply_symm_apply] at hmem
  obtain ⟨lift, hlift⟩ := hmem
  have hF : MapFiltrationAtLeast model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap 1 :=
    ⟨lift, hlift⟩
  change (if MapFiltrationAtLeast model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap 1 then 1 else 0) = 1
  exact if_pos hF
lean.statement:
public theorem eta_exponent :
  normalizedExponent model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap = 1

Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

The existential synthetic detection statement does not identify its witness with any separately chosen synthetic theta-five.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. Select the order-two 2-primary theta5 guaranteed by Xu, rather than asserting that every ordinary integral representative detected mod two has order two. Bidegrees (s,t)=(2,64) give synthetic (62,64). The existence of a prescribed-realization lift is derived using the project comparison theorem. This verifies the mathematical source and the stated adaptation, not the pending comparison with the fixed project model. No Lean proof obligation is discharged by this audit. Primary references: [BJMtheta5](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/barjoma.pdf): Theorem 2.1 and its immediate conclusion; pages [536, 537] [Xu](https://msp.org/gt/2016/20-3/gt-v20-n3-p08-p.pdf): Corollary 1.3; pages 1612 [IWX](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2001.04511v3): Corollary 1.3, Table 1, row k=62; pages [4, 6] [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 3.8(1), Proposition 3.11, and Notation 7.2; pages [16, 17, 42]

entries.label: sem:Literature:theta-indeterminacy
entries.title: The 2-primary stem and the filtration of choices
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{IWX}, Table 1; \cite{LWX126}, proof of Lem. 7.10.)\par{}

Every class $a\in\pi_{62}S^0$ annihilated by a power of two satisfies $2a=0$. If $a,b\in\pi_{62}S^0$ are detected by $h_5^2$, then $a-b$ has Adams filtration at least six.

    (∃ n : ℕ, (2 ^ n : ℕ) • a = 0) → a + a = 0 := by
  sorry
lean.docstring:
The ordinary 62-stem has exponent two on its 2-primary subgroup.
Odd-primary summands are not covered by this source obligation.
