comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The fixed h-zero choice is normalized by the first-quotient label and lambda[h-zero]=2, as in AimPaper Example 5.8(4). BHS Proposition A.20 gives a complete low synthetic ring presentation, with relation (0) h-zero eta=0 and relation (9) tau h-zero=2. In stem two, the presentation forces pi_(2,3) to be generated by tau eta^2 (the h-zero factors vanish), so h-zero annihilates every element there. This last assertion is a derived low-degree consequence, not a verbatim statement of AimPaper Lemma 7.16. The project must still identify its selected constants with these normalized low generators. Primary references: [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 7.3, Remarks 7.4–7.5; Example 5.8(4); proof of Lemma 7.16; pages 42, 28, 49–50; Repository AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf snapshot; no unstated version substitution [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Remark 9.5; Theorem A.8; Corollary A.9(1); Notation A.10, Corollary A.11; Proposition A.20, relations (0), (9), and Remark A.22; pages 32, 72–73, 78–79; published Acta page mapping supplied in bhs_pages/proposals.json; arXiv:1910.14116v3, as independently retrieved by the BHS audit worker

entries.title: A synthetic lift with prescribed realization
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(3b).)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical family, let $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ be a nonzero permanent label detecting $a\in\pi_{t-s}X$. There exists $b\in\pi_{t-s,t}\nu X$ with first-quotient label $x$ and realization equal to $a$.

public theorem selected_realization_prescribed_lift :
  ∀ (X : ClassicalObject) (s t : ℤ)
    (x : (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).Page 2 (s,t))
    (a : HomotopyGroup (t-s) (X.obj model.auxiliary)),
    NonzeroSurvival (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) (s,t) x →
    ClassicalDetects (model.classicalConvergence X) (s,t) x a →
    ∃ b : BiHom (t-s) t (nuZero model X), quotientClass 1 b = firstLabel model X s t x ∧
      realizeNu X b = a := by
  sorry

entries.title: A torsion lift of a boundary
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(3a).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $r\ge2$, and $y\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$. If $y$ has a common infinite-cycle representative and is hit on page $r$, there is $a\in\pi_{t-s,t}\nu X$ with first-quotient label $y$ and $\lambda^{r-1}a=0$.

entries.title: Adams filtration and lambda divisibility
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.19.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical family, integers $m,w,s$ with $w-m\le s$, and $a\in\pi_{m,w}\nu X$, the class $a$ has Adams filtration at least $s$ if and only if there is $b\in\pi_{m,m+s}\nu X$ with $\lambda^{m+s-w}b=a$.

entries.title: Detection of the finite-quotient action
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, Sec. 1; \cite{BHS}, Remark 9.5.)\par{}

Let $q>0$ and $s,t,s^{\prime},t^{\prime},k,l\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $x\in E_2^{s,t}(S^0)$ detects $a\in\pi_{t-s,t-k}S^{0,0}$ under the synthetic comparison, and the projected label of $y\in E_2^{s^{\prime},t^{\prime}}(S^0)$ detects $b\in\pi_{t^{\prime}-s^{\prime},t^{\prime}-l}(S^{0,0}/\lambda^q)$. Then the projected label of $xy$ detects $a\cdot b$ in tridegree $(s+s^{\prime},t+t^{\prime},t+t^{\prime}-k-l)$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.finite_action
lean.code:
public theorem finite_action (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (s t s' t' k l : ℕ)
    (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t))
    (y : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s',t'))
    (a : BiHom ((t : ℤ)-s) ((t : ℤ)-k) (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum))
    (b : BiHom ((t' : ℤ)-s') ((t' : ℤ)-l) (XModLambdaN (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) q))
    (ha : Detects (model.convergence .sphere) (s,t,(t : ℤ)-k) (model.comparison.sphereE2 s t k x) a)
    (hb : Detects (model.convergence (.quotient q .sphere)) (s',t',(t' : ℤ)-l)
      ((model.family.quotientProjection (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) q).pageMap 2
        (s',t',(t' : ℤ)-l) (model.comparison.sphereE2 s' t' l y)) b) :
    Detects (model.convergence (.quotient q .sphere))
      ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ)-(k+l : ℕ))
      ((model.family.quotientProjection (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) q).pageMap 2
        ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ)-(k+l : ℕ))
        (model.comparison.sphereE2 (s+s') (t+t') (k+l)

(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, Sec. 1; \cite{BHS}, Remark 9.5.)\par{}

Let $X$ lie in the chosen synthetic object family. For integers $m,w,m^{\prime},w^{\prime},s,s^{\prime}$, take $a\in\pi_{m,w}S^{0,0}$ and $b\in\pi_{m^{\prime},w^{\prime}}X$. entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(1a)--(1b).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $q>0$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$. The label $x$ reaches $E_{q+1}$ if and only if there is $a\in\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$ whose restriction to $\nu X/\lambda$ is the first-quotient class of $x$. Reaching a page permits zero and boundaries.

entries.title: Infinite representatives in a finite window
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.11.)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $q>0$, $0\le t-w<q$, $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ and $z\in E_\infty^{s,t,w}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$. The projected weight-$w$ label of $x$ represents $z$ if and only if $x\in Z_{q-t+w}^{s,t}(X)$ and the finite-window image of $z$ is the class of $x$ modulo $B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X)$.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.9(1)-(4), including its final surjectivity sentence; pages arXiv PDF pp. 72-73; published pp. 307-308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Proposition 3.11; pages local PDF p. 17; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical family and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$, the label $x$ has a common infinite-cycle representative if and only if there exists $a\in\pi_{t-s,t}\nu X$ with first-quotient label $x$. Zero labels are allowed.

entries.title: Products on the first quotient
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Thm. 4.46.)\par{}

Let $s,t,s^{\prime},t^{\prime}\in\mathbb N$ and let $x,y$ be first-quotient classes in bidegrees $(t-s,t)$ and $(t^{\prime}-s^{\prime},t^{\prime})$. The first-quotient image of their algebra product equals the Ext product of their images, in bidegree $(s+s^{\prime},t+t^{\prime})$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.quotientAlgebra_first_quotient
lean.code:
public theorem quotientAlgebra_first_quotient (s t s' t' : ℕ)
    (x : BiHom ((t : ℤ)-s) t (XModLambdaN (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) 1))
    (y : BiHom ((t' : ℤ)-s') t' (XModLambdaN (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) 1)) :
    KIP126.Literature.sphereFirstQuotient model ((s+s' : ℕ) : ℤ) ((t+t' : ℕ) : ℤ)
      (homotopyRegrade (by simp only [Nat.cast_add]; omega)
        (by simp only [Nat.cast_add]) (quotientAlgebraProduct (quotientAlgebra 1 (by decide)) x y)) =
      (eqToHom (congrArg (model.classical.sphere.Page 2)
        (show ((s : ℤ),(t : ℤ)) + ((s' : ℤ),(t' : ℤ)) = (((s+s' : ℕ) : ℤ),((t+t' : ℕ) : ℤ)) by
          simp only [Prod.mk_add_mk,Nat.cast_add])))
        (model.sphereAlgebra.product (s,t) (s',t')
          (KIP126.Literature.sphereFirstQuotient model s t x)
          (KIP126.Literature.sphereFirstQuotient model s' t' y)) := by
  sorry

comments.author: blueprint-authoring
comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.9(1)-(4), including its final surjectivity sentence; pages arXiv PDF pp. 72-73; published pp. 307-308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.11(1)-(3) and its proof; Notation A.10; pages arXiv PDF p. 73; published p. 308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Remark 3.14; pages local PDF p. 17; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Corollaries A.9 and A.11, and [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Remark 3.14.)

entries.title: Quotient multiplication and the sphere action
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Remark 3.4.)\par{}

Let $q>0$, $x\in\pi_{m,n}S^{0,0}$ and $y\in\pi_{k,l}(S^{0,0}/\lambda^q)$, with all four indices integral. Multiplication of the quotient image of $x$ by $y$ equals the sphere action $x\cdot y$.

entries.title: Realization of lambda and the unit
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.40.)\par{}

For all $m,w\in\mathbb Z$ and $k\in\mathbb N$, realization carries $\lambda^k:S^{m,w-k}\to S^{m,w}$ to the identity in sphere coordinates. At $(m,w)=(0,0)$, the sphere isomorphism agrees with the composite of the zero-shift identification, the inverse $\nu$--realization isomorphism, and the realization of the synthetic unit isomorphism.

entries.title: Restriction between finite infinite-page windows
entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Remark 3.14.)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $0<i\le j$, and $0\le t-w<i$. Under the infinite-page window equivalences, restriction $\nu X/\lambda^j\to\nu X/\lambda^i$ induces the natural map\[Z_{j-t+w}^{s,t}/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}\longrightarrow Z_{i-t+w}^{s,t}/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}.\]

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. entries.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(1c).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $q>0$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ reach $E_{q+1}$. There exists a lift $a\in\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$ restricting to the first-quotient class of $x$ such that the Bockstein label of $a$ represents $d_{q+1}x\in E_{q+1}^{s+q+1,t+q}(X)$.

BHS Proposition A.20 gives a complete low synthetic ring presentation, with relation (0) h-zero eta=0 and relation (9) tau h-zero=2. This last assertion is a derived low-degree consequence, not a verbatim statement of AimPaper Lemma 7.16. The project must still identify its selected constants with these normalized low generators. comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The public shift isomorphism includes integer pages below 2; those pages are frozen to the first page by a project convention, not covered as extra pages in the cited paper. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [Pst](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.01804v3): Definition 4.6; Definition 4.27; pages arXiv PDF pp. 39, 45; published pp. 609, 618; arXiv:1803.01804v3, 10 November 2022; numbering also checked in Invent. Math. 232 (2023) [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Theorem A.8; Notation A.6; pages arXiv PDF pp. 71-72; published pp. 306-307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7; pages local PDF p. 16; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

entries.title: Complete source coordinates
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and $t\leq261$, the source coordinates are a linear equivalence
\[P^{s,t}\cong\bigoplus_{i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)}\mathbb F_2.\]
The inverse of each coordinate unit vector is the value of the corresponding archived monomial. In particular, the archived monomials form a basis of $P^{s,t}$.

entries.label: sem:Computation:bounded-comparison
entries.title: The bounded comparison
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body: For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and $t\leq261$, the fixed comparison is a linear equivalence from $P^{s,t}$ to the actual sphere $E_2^{s,t}$. A sphere presentation requires the comparison to preserve the specified unit and every product of total degree $t+t\prime\leq261$, and to identify the selected $h_i$ with the fixed standard classes.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.SpherePresentation
lean.code:
public structure SpherePresentation (D : Model C Syn) (P : ProgramData.{v}) where
  comparison : ∀ s t : ℕ, t ≤ 261 →
    P.component s t ≃ₗ[ℤ] D.classical.sphere.Page 2 ((s : ℤ),(t : ℤ))
  comparison_product : ∀ s t s' t' : ℕ, ∀ h : t+t' ≤ 261,
    ∀ (x : P.component s t) (y : P.component s' t'),
    comparison (s+s') (t+t') h (P.product s t s' t' x y) =
      D.sphereAlgebra.product (s,t) (s',t')
        (comparison s t (by omega) x) (comparison s' t' (by omega) y)
  comparison_unit : comparison 0 0 (by decide) P.unit = D.sphereAlgebra.unit
  h0 : comparison 1 1 (by decide) (P.atom .h0) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 0
  h1 : comparison 1 2 (by decide) (P.atom .h1) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 1
  h2 : comparison 1 4 (by decide) (P.atom .h2) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 2
  h4 : comparison 1 16 (by decide) (P.atom .h4) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 4
  h5 : comparison 1 32 (by decide) (P.atom .h5) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 5
  h6 : comparison 1 64 (by decide) (P.atom .h6) = D.standardClasses.standardH6

entries.title: Products and the unit under comparison
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
If $t+t\prime\leq261$, then
\[c(xy)=c(x)c(y),\qquad c(1)=1.\]
The comparison is $\mathbb F_2$-linear.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.SpherePresentation.comparison_mul
lean.code:
public theorem comparison_mul (e : SpherePresentation D P) (s t s' t' : ℕ)
    (h : t+t' ≤ 261) (x : P.component s t) (y : P.component s' t') :

entries.label: sem:Computation:actual-coordinates
entries.title: Coordinates on the actual page
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
For $t\leq261$, composition of the inverse comparison with the source coordinates gives
\[E_2^{s,t}\cong\bigoplus_{i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)}\mathbb F_2.\]
Its inverse sends each unit vector to the image of the same archived monomial. Pulling that vector back by the comparison recovers the original source monomial.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.SpherePresentation.coordinates_basis
lean.code:
public theorem coordinates_basis (e : SpherePresentation D P)
    (S : SourceBasisSpecification P A) (s t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ 261)
    (i : Fin (A.basisCount s t)) :
    (e.coordinates S s t ht).symm (Finsupp.single i 1) =
      e.comparison s t ht ((A.basisMonomial s t i).value P S.generator) := by
  change e.comparison s t ht ((S.coordinates s t ht).symm (Finsupp.single i 1)) = _
  rw [S.basis_values]
lean.statement:
public theorem coordinates_basis (e : SpherePresentation D P)
    (S : SourceBasisSpecification P A) (s t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ 261)
    (i : Fin (A.basisCount s t)) :
    (e.coordinates S s t ht).symm (Finsupp.single i 1) =
      e.comparison s t ht ((A.basisMonomial s t i).value P S.generator)
lean.docstring:
Every actual coordinate unit vector is the image of the same archived
monomial, not a freshly selected basis of the same dimension.

public theorem h6_square (e : SpherePresentation D P) :
    e.comparison 2 128 (by decide)
      (P.product 1 64 1 64 (P.atom .h6) (P.atom .h6)) =
      D.standardClasses.standardH6Square := by
  have h := e.comparison_mul 1 64 1 64 (by decide) (P.atom .h6) (P.atom .h6)
  change e.comparison 2 128 _ (P.product 1 64 1 64 (P.atom .h6) (P.atom .h6)) =
    D.sphereAlgebra.product (1,64) (1,64)
      (e.comparison 1 64 _ (P.atom .h6)) (e.comparison 1 64 _ (P.atom .h6)) at h
  rw [e.h6] at h
  exact h

entries.label: sem:Computation:top-cell-comparison
entries.title: Identification of the top-cell image
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived nu-cofiber comparison.)\par
The image of $a$ under the actual cofiber connecting arrow desuspends, through the prescribed four sphere suspensions and shift coherence maps, to $X=h_1x_{121,7}$. The comparison supplies the intermediate labels in degrees $(8,133)$, $(8,132)$ and $(8,131)$.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.Standard.top_comparison
lean.code:
public theorem top_comparison :
  ∃ (a3 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 3)).Page 2 (8,133))
    (a2 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 2)).Page 2 (8,132))
    (a1 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 1)).Page 2 (8,131)),
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 3 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 134
      (model.classical.pageMap (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibδ model.auxiliary.nuMap) 2 (8,134) topCell) a3 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 2 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 133
      (model.classical.pageMap
        ((shiftFunctorAdd' Spectrum (2 : ℤ) 1 3 (by decide)).hom.app SphereSpectrum)
        2 (8,133) a3) a2 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 1 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 132
      (model.classical.pageMap
        ((shiftFunctorAdd' Spectrum (1 : ℤ) 1 2 (by decide)).hom.app SphereSpectrum)
        2 (8,132) a2) a1 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension .sphere).DesuspendsClass 8 131 a1 X := by sorry
lean.statement:
public theorem top_comparison :
  ∃ (a3 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 3)).Page 2 (8,133))
    (a2 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 2)).Page 2 (8,132))
    (a1 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 1)).Page 2 (8,131)),
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 3 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 134
      (model.classical.pageMap (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibδ model.auxiliary.nuMap) 2 (8,134) topCell) a3 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 2 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 133
      (model.classical.pageMap
        ((shiftFunctorAdd' Spectrum (2 : ℤ) 1 3 (by decide)).hom.app SphereSpectrum)
        2 (8,133) a3) a2 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 1 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 132
      (model.classical.pageMap
        ((shiftFunctorAdd' Spectrum (1 : ℤ) 1 2 (by decide)).hom.app SphereSpectrum)
        2 (8,132) a2) a1 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension .sphere).DesuspendsClass 8 131 a1 X
lean.docstring:
The selected label is tied to the actual connecting arrow and four
specified sphere desuspensions.

entries.title: Finite table coordinates
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived finite tables.)\par
A table row specifies the sphere or $C\nu$, an Adams bidegree and an increasing list of coordinate indices. A row is coordinate-valid if its degree occurs in the table and its coordinate indices are strictly increasing and less than the tabulated dimension.

entries.label: sem:Computation:table-realization
entries.title: Realization and decoding of a table row
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
For $o=S^0$ or $C\nu$, write $b_{o;s,t,i}\in E_2^{s,t}(o)$ for the specified basis vectors. For the sphere, $t\leq261$ and $i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)$, these are the inverse coordinate images of the unit vectors; set $b_{S^0;s,t,i}=0$ when either bound fails. A coordinate-valid list $I$ represents
\[\sum_{i\in I}b_{o;s,t,i}.\]
An invalid coordinate list represents no element. The basis is complete if there is a linear coordinate equivalence sending every $b_{o;s,t,i}$ to the corresponding unit vector.

lean.code:
public theorem basis_correct (d : Raw.Degree) (hd : d ∈ Raw.degrees) : BasisCorrect d := by
  rcases d with ⟨o,s,t,ms⟩
  cases o with
  | sphere =>
    have hc := basis_count ⟨.sphere,s,t,ms⟩ hd rfl
    have ht := table_degree_bound ⟨.sphere,s,t,ms⟩ hd
    dsimp only at hc ht
    change ∃ e : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t) ≃ₗ[ℤ] (Fin ms.length →₀ ZMod 2),
      ∀ i, e.symm (Finsupp.single i 1) = sphereBasis s t i.val
    rw [← hc]
    refine ⟨Standard.coordinates s t ht, ?_⟩
    intro i
    simp only [sphereBasis, dif_pos ht, dif_pos i.isLt]
  | nuCofiber => exact cofiber_basis_correct ⟨.nuCofiber,s,t,ms⟩ hd rfl

entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body: Let $G_{j;s,t}$ be the image in $E_2^{s,t}$ of archived generator $j$ when $t\leq261$ and $j$ has bidegree $(s,t)$, and set $G_{j;s,t}=0$ otherwise. For each basis-value record $(e,i)$, the $i$th basis vector in the bidegree of $e$ equals the value of $e$.

public def generatorImage (id s t : ℕ) : Page .sphere s t :=
  if ht : t ≤ 261 then
    if hi : id < Standard.archive.generators.count then
      if hd : Standard.archive.generators.degree ⟨id,hi⟩ = (s,t) then
        Standard.comparison s t ht
          ((eqToHom (congrArg (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => Standard.sourceData.component p.1 p.2) hd))
            (Standard.sourceGenerator ⟨id,hi⟩))
      else 0
    else 0
  else 0

entries.body:
The sphere basis vectors satisfy
\[b_{S^0;11,133,1}=P,\qquad b_{S^0;12,134,0}=Q,\qquad b_{S^0;14,139,1}=T,\]
\[b_{S^0;10,134,4}=U,\qquad b_{S^0;13,137,1}=C,\qquad b_{S^0;13,137,2}=h_4x_{109,12}.\]
If $x\in E_2^{s,t}$, $y\in E_2^{s\prime,t\prime}$ and $t+t\prime\leq261$, then $xy=yx$. Moreover, $h_0h_1=h_1h_2=0$.

entries.label: sem:E2Computation:two-line-exhaustive
entries.title: Exhaustive standard products on the Adams second line
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Adams60}, Theorem 2.5.1(2), p.~45.)\par{}

For every integer $t$ and nonzero $x\in E_2^{2,t}(S^0)$, there are natural numbers $i\leq j$ and a bidegree equation
\[
 (1,2^i)+(1,2^j)=(2,t)
\]
such that $x$ equals the corresponding transport of $H_{i,j}$. There is no upper bound on $t$, $i$ or $j$.

lean.name: KIP126.E2Computation.two_line_exhaustive
lean.code:
public theorem two_line_exhaustive (t : ℤ) (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (2,t))
    (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ i j : ℕ, i ≤ j ∧
      ∃ degree : hiDegree i + hiDegree j = (2,t),
        x = (eqToHom (congrArg (ActualE2At model.classical) degree))
          (KIP126.Literature.Standard.hiProduct i j) := by
  sorry
lean.statement:
public theorem two_line_exhaustive (t : ℤ) (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (2,t))
    (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ i j : ℕ, i ≤ j ∧
      ∃ degree : hiDegree i + hiDegree j = (2,t),
        x = (eqToHom (congrArg (ActualE2At model.classical) degree))
          (KIP126.Literature.Standard.hiProduct i j)
lean.docstring:
Every nonzero homogeneous second-line element is a standard product.
The degree equation and equality are in the actual fixed E₂ module.

comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Original source checked directly: [Adams60](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970147), Theorem 2.5.1(2), pp.~44--45, gives the second-line basis h_j h_i for j>=i>=0 and j!=i+1. [LinExt4](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.topol.2007.11.003), Theorem 1.2, p.~460, recalls this earlier result and is not its original source. Distinct ordered power-of-two pairs have distinct sums, so each nonzero homogeneous element over F2 is a single basis product. The theorem is adapted to integer grading, actual page products and their degree transports. Identification of the abstract Ext basis with the project's fixed E2 product remains the registered E2Computation obligation; this source check does not prove it. The finite archive bound t<=261 is not extrapolated. Primary text: [Adams](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Adams-HI1.pdf), Theorem 2.5.1(2), p.45.

entries.label: frontier:E2Computation:1652f2bec247
entries.title: Commutativity of bounded sphere products
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
For $s,t,s',t'\in\mathbb N$ with $t+t'\leq261$, $x\in E_2^{s,t}(S^0)$ and $y\in E_2^{s',t'}(S^0)$,
\[xy=yx\in E_2^{s+s',t+t'}(S^0),\]
using the canonical identifications of the two sums of bidegrees.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.Table.product_comm
lean.code:
public theorem product_comm (s t s' t' : ℕ) (ht : t+t' ≤ 261)
    (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t))
    (y : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s',t')) :
    Standard.product (r := ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ))) x y
        (by simp only [Prod.mk_add_mk,Nat.cast_add]) =
      Standard.product (r := ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ))) y x
        (by simp only [Prod.mk_add_mk,Nat.cast_add]; ext <;> omega) := by
  sorry
lean.statement:
public theorem product_comm (s t s' t' : ℕ) (ht : t+t' ≤ 261)
    (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t))
    (y : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s',t')) :
    Standard.product (r := ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ))) x y
        (by simp only [Prod.mk_add_mk,Nat.cast_add]) =
      Standard.product (r := ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ))) y x
        (by simp only [Prod.mk_add_mk,Nat.cast_add]; ext <;> omega)
lean.docstring:
The original commutative source algebra, transported by the same bounded
comparison. This retains the total-degree bound of comparison_product.

entries.title: The top-cell comparison and a product relation
entries.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
entries.body:
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\delta:C\nu\to S^3[1]$ be the cofiber connecting map, and let $\sigma_{j,1}:S^j[1]\cong S^{j+1}$ be the fixed shift-coherence isomorphisms. There are classes
\[a_3\in E_2^{8,133}(S^3),\quad a_2\in E_2^{8,132}(S^2),\quad a_1\in E_2^{8,131}(S^1)\]
such that $\delta_*a$ desuspends to $a_3$, $(\sigma_{2,1}^{-1})_*a_3$ desuspends to $a_2$, $(\sigma_{1,1}^{-1})_*a_2$ desuspends to $a_1$, and $a_1$ desuspends to $X$. These are the four fixed sphere desuspension relations.
\item $Xh_2=0\in E_2^{9,134}(S^0)$.
\end{enumerate}

lean.code:
public theorem top_comparison :
  ∃ (a3 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 3)).Page 2 (8,133))
    (a2 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 2)).Page 2 (8,132))
    (a1 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 1)).Page 2 (8,131)),
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 3 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 134
      (model.classical.pageMap (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibδ model.auxiliary.nuMap) 2 (8,134) topCell) a3 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 2 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 133
      (model.classical.pageMap
        ((shiftFunctorAdd' Spectrum (2 : ℤ) 1 3 (by decide)).hom.app SphereSpectrum)
        2 (8,133) a3) a2 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 1 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 132
      (model.classical.pageMap
        ((shiftFunctorAdd' Spectrum (1 : ℤ) 1 2 (by decide)).hom.app SphereSpectrum)
        2 (8,132) a2) a1 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension .sphere).DesuspendsClass 8 131 a1 X := by sorry

    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 3 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 134

entries.body: For a classical spectrum $X$, a common label in bidegree $(s,t)$ is an element of $E_2^{s,t}(X)$. For $c\geq1$, it is a level-$c$ cycle, respectively boundary, if it lies in $Z_c^{s,t}(X)$, respectively $B_c^{s,t}(X)$. - **exclusions**: Treating a paper-specific conclusion or local Moss application as an upstream external premise.

- **exclusions**: Claiming archived source text, hashes or successful compilation certify completed formal proofs.

- **exclusions**: Restoring Challenge/result-package parameters or adding geometric Kervaire goals.

- **scope.finite_stretching**: The frozen baseline provides a layer-preserving strengthened sufficient condition for existence of a later finite-page extension. It excludes finite nonliftable crossings, including inessential ones; it is not claimed equivalent to the full printed paper criterion. It does not assert lifting an arbitrary chosen strict solution, an infinite compatible lift tower, or an untruncated extension.

entries.title: Congruence and differential equations
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body: For $c\geq1$, labels $x,y\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ are congruent at level $c$ if $x-y\in B_c^{s,t}(X)$. For $r\geq2$, the equation $d_r(x)=y$ means that $x$ and $y$ represent classes on page $r$ and their classes satisfy the Adams differential equation, with source bidegree $(s,t)$ and target bidegree $(s+r,t+r-1)$. The target may be zero.

entries.title: Cycles and representatives on later pages
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body: For $r\geq2$, a common label lies in $Z_{r-1}$ if and only if it reaches page $r$. If $x$ represents $x_r$ on page $r$ and $y-x\in B_{r-1}$, then $y$ represents $x_r$. If $d_r(x)=y$ and $y'-y\in B_{r-1}$, then $d_r(x)=y'$.

lean.code:
public theorem differentialAt_of_congruent (X : ClassicalObject) {R : ℤ}
    {p q : ℤ × ℤ} {x : Ambient D X p} {y z : Ambient D X q}
    (hd : DifferentialAt D X R p q x y)
    (hz : Congruent D X (R - 1) q z y) :
    DifferentialAt D X R p q x z := by
  obtain ⟨hR, hdeg, xr, yr, hx, hy, hdiff⟩ := hd
  exact ⟨hR, hdeg, xr, yr, hx, representsOnPage_of_congruent D X hR hy hz, hdiff⟩

  let E := D.classical.obj (X.obj D.auxiliary)
  let P := E.ssData p
  let m : WithTop ℕ := ↑(r-E.r₀).toNat
  have hm : (↑(r-1-1).toNat : WithTop ℕ) = m := by
    dsimp only [m, E]
    rw [D.classical.firstPage]
    congr 2; omega
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨_, hx⟩
    change ∃ z, KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel D X (↑(r-1-1).toNat) p z = x at hx
    rw [hm] at hx
    obtain ⟨z,hz⟩ := hx
    refine ⟨P.pageπ m z, hr, z, ?_, rfl⟩
    change (Subobject.ofLE (P.Z m) (P.Z _) _ ≫ P.pageπ _) z = x
    rw [initialProjection_eq_cycleLabel D X r hr p]
    exact hz
  · rintro ⟨y, _, z, hz, _⟩
    refine ⟨by omega, ?_⟩
    change ∃ z, KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel D X (↑(r-1-1).toNat) p z = x
    rw [hm]
    refine ⟨z, ?_⟩
    rw [initialProjection_eq_cycleLabel D X r hr p] at hz
    exact hz

public theorem representsOnPage_of_congruent (X : ClassicalObject) {R : ℤ}
    (hR : 2 ≤ R) {p : ℤ × ℤ} {x y : Ambient D X p}
    {xr : (D.classical.obj (X.obj D.auxiliary)).Page R p}
    (hx : RepresentsOnPage (D.classical.obj (X.obj D.auxiliary)) R p x xr)
    (hy : Congruent D X (R - 1) p y x) :
    RepresentsOnPage (D.classical.obj (X.obj D.auxiliary)) R p y xr := by
  let E := D.classical.obj (X.obj D.auxiliary)
  let P := E.ssData p
  let k : WithTop ℕ := ↑(R - E.r₀).toNat
  obtain ⟨_, z, hzx, hzr⟩ := hx
  have hb : y - x ∈ KIP126.Literature.boundaries D X (R - 1) p := hy.2
  change ∃ b, KIP126.Literature.boundaryLabel D X (↑(R - 1 - 1).toNat) p b = y - x at hb
  have hk : (↑(R-1-1).toNat : WithTop ℕ) = k := by
    dsimp only [k,E]
    rw [D.classical.firstPage]
    congr 2; omega
  rw [hk] at hb
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hb
  let j := Subobject.ofLE (P.B k) (P.Z k) (P.B_le_Z k)
  have hlabel : j ≫ KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel D X k p =
      KIP126.Literature.boundaryLabel D X k p := by
    dsimp only [j, KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel, KIP126.Literature.boundaryLabel, P, E]
    simp only [← Category.assoc, Subobject.ofLE_comp_ofLE]
  have hboundary : (P.pageπ k) (j b) = 0 := by
    have hj : j ≫ P.pageπ k = 0 := cokernel.condition _
    exact congrArg (fun f => f b) hj
  refine ⟨hR, z + j b, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have hz0 : KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel D X k p z = x := by
      rw [initialProjection_eq_cycleLabel D X R hR p] at hzx
      exact hzx
    have hzb : KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel D X k p (j b) = y - x := by
      change (j ≫ KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel D X k p) b = _
      rw [hlabel]
      exact hb
    have hh : KIP126.Literature.cycleLabel D X k p (z + j b) = y := by
      rw [map_add, hz0, hzb]
      abel
    change (Subobject.ofLE (P.Z k) (P.Z _) _ ≫ P.pageπ _) (z+j b) = y
    rw [initialProjection_eq_cycleLabel D X R hR p]
    exact hh
  · change P.pageπ k (z + j b) = xr
    rw [map_add, hboundary, add_zero]
    exact hzr

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-correction
entries.title: Finite correction of a residual
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Let $A,A',B$ be abelian groups, $N\in\mathbb N$, and $\rho:A'\to A$ and $g:A\to B$ homomorphisms, let $E_k\leq A$, $L_k\leq A'$ with $L$ decreasing, and let $T\leq B$. Suppose that for each $s\leq k<s+N$, a residual $\delta\in E_k$ can either be corrected by some $\varepsilon\in L_k$ so that $\delta-\rho\varepsilon\in E_{k+1}$, or already satisfies $g\delta\in T$. Suppose also that $g(E_{s+N})\subseteq T$. If $\alpha_0-\rho\alpha\in E_s$, there is $\alpha'$ with
\[\alpha'-\alpha\in L_s,\qquad g(\alpha_0-\rho\alpha')\in T.\]

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.finite_filtration_correction
lean.code:
public theorem finite_filtration_correction
    {A A' B : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] [AddCommGroup A'] [AddCommGroup B]
    (ρ : A' →+ A) (g : A →+ B)
    (E : ℤ → AddSubgroup A) (L : ℤ → AddSubgroup A')
    (T : AddSubgroup B) (hL : Antitone L)
    (s : ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hstep : ∀ k : ℤ, s ≤ k → k < s + N → ∀ δ : A, δ ∈ E k →
      (∃ ε : A', ε ∈ L k ∧ δ - ρ ε ∈ E (k + 1)) ∨ g δ ∈ T)
    (hend : ∀ δ : A, δ ∈ E (s + N) → g δ ∈ T)
    (α₀ : A) (α : A') (hδ : α₀ - ρ α ∈ E s) :
    ∃ α' : A', α' - α ∈ L s ∧ g (α₀ - ρ α') ∈ T := by
  induction N generalizing s α with
  | zero =>
    refine ⟨α, ?_, hend _ ?_⟩
    · simpa only [sub_self] using (L s).zero_mem
    · simpa only [Nat.cast_zero, add_zero] using hδ
  | succ N ih =>
    rcases hstep s le_rfl (by omega) _ hδ with hcorrect | hstop
    · obtain ⟨ε, hε, hδε⟩ := hcorrect
      have hδ' : α₀ - ρ (α + ε) ∈ E (s + 1) := by
        simpa only [map_add, sub_add_eq_sub_sub] using hδε
      obtain ⟨α', hα', hfinal⟩ := ih (s + 1)
        (fun k hk hkn δ hδ => hstep k (by omega) (by omega) δ hδ)
        (fun δ hδ => hend δ (by simpa only [Nat.cast_succ, add_assoc,
          add_comm, add_left_comm] using hδ)) (α + ε) hδ'
      refine ⟨α', ?_, hfinal⟩
      have hmem := (L s).add_mem (hL (by omega) hα') hε
      convert hmem using 1
      abel
    · exact ⟨α, by simpa only [sub_self] using (L s).zero_mem, hstop⟩
lean.statement:
public theorem finite_filtration_correction
    {A A' B : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] [AddCommGroup A'] [AddCommGroup B]
    (ρ : A' →+ A) (g : A →+ B)
    (E : ℤ → AddSubgroup A) (L : ℤ → AddSubgroup A')
    (T : AddSubgroup B) (hL : Antitone L)
    (s : ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hstep : ∀ k : ℤ, s ≤ k → k < s + N → ∀ δ : A, δ ∈ E k →
      (∃ ε : A', ε ∈ L k ∧ δ - ρ ε ∈ E (k + 1)) ∨ g δ ∈ T)
    (hend : ∀ δ : A, δ ∈ E (s + N) → g δ ∈ T)
    (α₀ : A) (α : A') (hδ : α₀ - ρ α ∈ E s) :
    ∃ α' : A', α' - α ∈ L s ∧ g (α₀ - ρ α') ∈ T

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-reflection
entries.title: Reflection along a finite filtration interval
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body: Let $B',B$ be abelian groups, $N\in\mathbb N$, and $\rho:B'\to B$ a homomorphism. Let $E$ be a decreasing filtration on $B$, and let $L_k\leq B'$. Suppose that for $s\leq k<s+N$, $b\in L_k$ and $\rho b\in E_{k+1}$ imply $b\in L_{k+1}$. Then $b\in L_s$ and $\rho b\in E_{s+N}$ imply $b\in L_{s+N}$.

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.finite_filtration_reflection
lean.code:
public theorem finite_filtration_reflection
    {B' B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B'] [AddCommGroup B]
    (ρ : B' →+ B) (L : ℤ → AddSubgroup B') (E : ℤ → AddSubgroup B)
    (hE : Antitone E) (s : ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hgraded : ∀ k : ℤ, s ≤ k → k < s + N → ∀ b : B', b ∈ L k →
      ρ b ∈ E (k + 1) → b ∈ L (k + 1))
    (b : B') (hb : b ∈ L s) (hρb : ρ b ∈ E (s + N)) :
    b ∈ L (s + N) := by
  have h : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → b ∈ L (s + k) := by
    intro k hk
    induction k with
    | zero => simpa only [Nat.cast_zero, add_zero] using hb
    | succ k ih =>
      have hkN : k ≤ N := by omega
      have hnext := hgraded (s + k) (by omega) (by omega) b (ih hkN)
        (hE (by omega) hρb)
      simpa only [Nat.cast_succ, add_assoc] using hnext
  exact h N le_rfl
lean.statement:
public theorem finite_filtration_reflection
    {B' B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B'] [AddCommGroup B]
    (ρ : B' →+ B) (L : ℤ → AddSubgroup B') (E : ℤ → AddSubgroup B)
    (hE : Antitone E) (s : ℤ) (N : ℕ)
    (hgraded : ∀ k : ℤ, s ≤ k → k < s + N → ∀ b : B', b ∈ L k →
      ρ b ∈ E (k + 1) → b ∈ L (k + 1))
    (b : B') (hb : b ∈ L s) (hρb : ρ b ∈ E (s + N)) :
    b ∈ L (s + N)

filtration interval; it does not require injectivity of the ambient map.

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:leading-grade
entries.title: The first nonzero grade in a finite interval
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Let $E_k$ be subgroups of an abelian group and let $N\in\mathbb N$. If $b\in E_s$ but $b\notin E_{s+N}$, then there exists $s\leq k<s+N$ with
\[b\in E_k\quad\text{and}\quad b\notin E_{k+1}.\]

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.first_nonzero_filtration_grade
lean.code:
public theorem first_nonzero_filtration_grade
    {B : Type*} [AddCommGroup B] (E : ℤ → AddSubgroup B)
    (s : ℤ) (N : ℕ) (b : B) (hb : b ∈ E s) (hnot : b ∉ E (s + N)) :
    ∃ k : ℤ, s ≤ k ∧ k < s + N ∧ b ∈ E k ∧ b ∉ E (k + 1) := by
  induction N generalizing s with
  | zero => exact (hnot (by simpa only [Nat.cast_zero, add_zero] using hb)).elim
  | succ N ih =>
    by_cases hnext : b ∈ E (s + 1)
    · have hnot' : b ∉ E ((s + 1) + N) := by
        simpa only [Nat.cast_succ, add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using hnot
      obtain ⟨k, hk, hkN, hb, hnot⟩ := ih (s + 1) hnext hnot'

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:extension-representatives
entries.title: Representatives for a tower extension equation
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be a map of convergent towers. Fix $(m,w)$ and classes $x\in E_\infty^{s,m+s,w}(X)$ and $y\in E_\infty^{s+n,m+s+n,w}(Y)$. An extension equation of length $n$ from $x$ to $y$ holds if and only if $n\geq0$ and there are representatives
\[a\in F^s\pi_{m,w}X,\qquad b\in F^{s+n}\pi_{m,w}Y,\qquad g_*(a)=b\]
whose associated-graded classes correspond to $x$ and $y$ under the convergence isomorphisms.

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.Operations.tower_extension_iff
lean.code:
public theorem tower_extension_iff
    {Syn : Type u} [SyntheticCategory.{u,v} Syn]
    [KIP126.StableHomotopy.HasFunctorialCofiber (C := Syn)]
    {H : Syn} {unit : S_0_0 ⟶ H} {F : SyntheticAdamsFamily Syn}
    {P : SyntheticTowerPresentation unit F} {X Y : Syn} {g : X ⟶ Y}
    {cx : SyntheticTowerConvergence P X} {cy : SyntheticTowerConvergence P Y}
    (M : ConvergentMap F g cx.toConvergence cy.toConvergence)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s n : ℤ)
    (x : ((F.obj X).sequence.ssData (s,p.1+s,p.2)).eInfty)
    (y : ((F.obj Y).sequence.ssData (s+n,p.1+(s+n),p.2)).eInfty) :
    TowerExtensionEquation M p s n x y ↔
      0 ≤ n ∧ ∃ (a : (Subobject.underlying.obj ((P.filtration X).F s p) : ModuleCat.{v} ℤ))
        (b : (Subobject.underlying.obj ((P.filtration Y).F (s+n) p) : ModuleCat.{v} ℤ)),
        ((P.filtration X).F s p).arrow a ≫ g = ((P.filtration Y).F (s+n) p).arrow b ∧
        (P.filtration X).toAssociatedGraded s p a = (infinityGradedIso cx p s).hom x ∧
        (P.filtration Y).toAssociatedGraded (s+n) p b = (infinityGradedIso cy p (s+n)).hom y :=
  Internal.tower_extension_iff M p s n x y

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:grade-naturality
entries.title: Naturality and the next-filtration ambiguity
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be a map of convergent towers, $a\in F^s\pi_{m,w}X$ and $b\in F^s\pi_{m,w}Y$. If $g_*(a)=b$, their associated-graded classes satisfy $g_\infty([a])=[b]$. Conversely, this graded equality implies
\[b-g_*(a)\in F^{s+1}\pi_{m,w}Y.\]
If $g_\infty$ is injective in this degree and $g_*(a)\in F^{s+1}\pi_{m,w}Y$, then $a\in F^{s+1}\pi_{m,w}X$.

entries.title: The finite quotient strip
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
For $q>0$, the infinite page of $
u X/\lambda^q$ vanishes outside $0\leq t-w<q$. Every $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t}(
u X/\lambda^q)$ has filtration at least $s$. If $q\leq m+s-w$, an element of $\pi_{m,w}(
u X/\lambda^q)$ in filtration at least $s$ is zero.

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-target-label
entries.title: Finite target labels
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
For $q>0$ and $0\leq k<q$, let $y\in Z_{q-k}^{s,t}(X)$. Its finite target label at weight $t-k$ represents $e\in E_\infty^{s,t,t-k}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$ if and only if the finite-window comparison carries $e$ to the class of $y$ in
\[Z_{q-k}^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+k}^{s,t}(X).\]

public theorem finite_target_label_iff (X : ClassicalObject) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q)
    (s t : ℤ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k < q)
    (y : cycles model X ((q:ℤ)-t+(t-k)) (s,t))
    (e : ((model.family.quotient (model.nu.functor.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) q).sequence.ssData
      (s,t,t-k)).eInfty) :
    HasInfinityRepresentative _ 2 (s,t,t-k) (finiteTargetLabel model X q s t k y.val) e ↔
      KIP126.Literature.Standard.infinityFiniteWindow X q hq (s,t) (t-k) (by omega) e =
        subquotientClass (cycles model X ((q:ℤ)-t+(t-k)) (s,t))
          (boundaries model X (1+t-(t-k)) (s,t)) y := by
  exact Internal.Mahowald.finite_target_label_iff X q hq s t k hk y e

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:shift-coherence
entries.title: Suspension and composition coherence
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Assume that suspension and bigraded shifts are coherent with the homotopy functors. The canonical isomorphism
\[\Sigma^{1,-q}Q\cong\Sigma(\Sigma^{0,-q}Q)\]
identifies the induced suspension and bigraded-shift maps. The inverse and composition isomorphisms for shifts induce the corresponding inverse and composition maps on homotopy groups.

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:leibniz-law
entries.title: The generalized Leibniz law
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ and write $e=e(f)$. The generalized Leibniz law is the following implication. Assume $2\leq p\leq r$, $e\leq m\leq p-2+e$, $e\leq l$, and
\[x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(X),\qquad y\in Z_{r-1-m+e}^{s+m,t+m}(Y),\]
\[x_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(X),\qquad y_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r+l,t+r+l-1}(Y).\]
Suppose that
\[d_r(x)=x_\infty,\qquad d_m^{f,E_p}(x)=y,\qquad d_l^{f,E_\infty}(x_\infty)=y_\infty.\]
Assume either that the first differential has no crossing on page $p$ or that the finite extension has no crossing, and assume that the infinite extension has no crossing. Then
\[d_{r+l-m}(y)=y_\infty.\]

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.GeneralizedLeibnizLaw
lean.code:
public def GeneralizedLeibnizLaw (X Y : ClassicalObject) (f : X.obj D.auxiliary ⟶ Y.obj D.auxiliary) : Prop :=
  ∀ (page : ℕ) (r m l s t : ℤ)
    (x : Ambient D X (s, t)) (y : Ambient D Y (s + m, t + m))
    (xInfinity : Ambient D X (s + r, t + r - 1))
    (yInfinity : Ambient D Y (s + r + l, t + r - 1 + l)),
    2 ≤ page → (page : ℤ) ≤ r →
    (normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f : ℤ) ≤ m →
    m ≤ (page : ℤ) - 2 + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f →
    (normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f : ℤ) ≤ l →
    IsCycle D X (r - 1) (s, t) x →
    IsCycle D Y (r - 1 - m + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f) (s + m, t + m) y →
    IsPermanent D X (s + r, t + r - 1) xInfinity →
    IsPermanent D Y (s + r + l, t + r - 1 + l) yInfinity →
    DifferentialAt D X r (s, t) (s + r, t + r - 1) x xInfinity →
    FiniteExtension D X Y f page m s t x y →
    InfiniteExtension D X Y f l (s + r) (t + r - 1) xInfinity yInfinity →
    (NoCrossingOn D X r page (s, t) ∨
      FiniteNoCrossing D X Y f page m s t) →
    InfiniteNoCrossing D X Y f l (s + r) (t + r - 1) →
    DifferentialAt D Y (r + l - m) (s + m, t + m)
      (s + r + l, t + r - 1 + l) y yInfinity

    (xInfinity : Ambient D X (s + r, t + r - 1))

论文中的 δ／λ／ρ 推理。不要求微分或 extension 非零。

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:mahowald-law
entries.title: The normalized-triangle Mahowald law
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow h\Sigma X$ be a distinguished triangle with $e(f)+e(g)+e(h)=1$, whose normalized synthetic maps form a compatible triangle. Put
\[n_1=n-e(f)\geq1,\quad m_1=m-e(g)\geq0,\quad l_1=l-e(h)\geq0,\quad r=n+m+l,\quad r'=r-m_1.\]
The normalized-triangle Mahowald law is the following implication. Suppose
\[x\in Z_{n_1}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X),\quad y\in Z_{m_1+1}^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y),\]
\[\bar x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(Z),\qquad\bar y\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(Z).\]
Let $\widetilde x\in E_2^{s+l,t+l}(\Sigma X)$ desuspend to $x$ under the tower suspension comparison, and assume
\[d_l^{h,E_{r'}}(\bar x)=\widetilde x,\qquad d_r(\bar x)=\bar y,\qquad d_m^{g,E_{m_1+2}}(y)=\bar y.\]
Assume that the $h$-extension has no crossing or that the classical differential has no crossing on page $r'$. Then $x\in Z_{n+m+e(h)}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X)$ and there is $y'$ such that
\[d_n^{f,E_{n+m+1+e(h)}}(x)=y',\qquad y'-y\in B_{r'}^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y).\]

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.GeneralizedMahowaldLaw
lean.code:
public def GeneralizedMahowaldLaw (T : TriangleData D.auxiliary) : Prop :=
  ∀ he : (normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.f : ℤ) + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.g +
      normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.h = 1,
  KIP126.Literature.NormalizedTriangleCompatible D T he →
  ∀ (n m l s t : ℤ),
    let r := n + m + l
    let n₁ := n - normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.f
    let m₁ := m - normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.g
    let l₁ := l - normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.h
    let r' := r - m₁
    ∀ (x : Ambient D (T.X) (s + l, t + l - 1))
      (y : Ambient D (T.Y) (s + l + n, t + l - 1 + n))
      (xBar : Ambient D (T.Z) (s, t))
      (yBar : Ambient D (T.Z) (s + l + n + m, t + l - 1 + n + m))
      (suspendedX : Ambient D (.shift 1 T.X) (s + l, t + l)),
      1 ≤ n₁ → 0 ≤ m₁ → 0 ≤ l₁ →
      IsCycle D (T.X) n₁ (s + l, t + l - 1) x →
      IsCycle D (T.Y) (m₁ + 1) (s + l + n, t + l - 1 + n) y →
      IsCycle D (T.Z) (r - 1) (s, t) xBar →
      IsPermanent D (T.Z) (s + l + n + m, t + l - 1 + n + m) yBar →
      (D.classicalSuspension T.X).DesuspendsClass (s + l) (t + l) suspendedX x →
      FiniteExtension D T.Z (.shift 1 T.X) T.h r'.toNat l s t xBar suspendedX →
      DifferentialAt D (T.Z) r (s, t)
        (s + l + n + m, t + l - 1 + n + m) xBar yBar →
      (FiniteNoCrossing D T.Z (.shift 1 T.X) T.h r'.toNat l s t ∨
        NoCrossingOn D (T.Z) r r' (s, t)) →
      FiniteExtension D T.Y T.Z T.g (m₁ + 2).toNat m (s + l + n) (t + l - 1 + n) y yBar →
      IsCycle D (T.X) (n + m + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.h) (s + l, t + l - 1) x ∧
        ∃ y' : Ambient D (T.Y) (s + l + n, t + l - 1 + n),
          FiniteExtension D T.X T.Y T.f (n + m + 1 + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.h).toNat
            n (s + l) (t + l - 1) x y' ∧
          Congruent D (T.Y) r' (s + l + n, t + l - 1 + n) y' y

    let m₁ := m - normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.g
    let l₁ := l - normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.h
    let r' := r - m₁

      (xBar : Ambient D (T.Z) (s, t))
      (yBar : Ambient D (T.Z) (s + l + n + m, t + l - 1 + n + m))
      (suspendedX : Ambient D (.shift 1 T.X) (s + l, t + l)),
      1 ≤ n₁ → 0 ≤ m₁ → 0 ≤ l₁ →
      IsCycle D (T.X) n₁ (s + l, t + l - 1) x →
      IsCycle D (T.Y) (m₁ + 1) (s + l + n, t + l - 1 + n) y →
      IsCycle D (T.Z) (r - 1) (s, t) xBar →
      IsPermanent D (T.Z) (s + l + n + m, t + l - 1 + n + m) yBar →
      (D.classicalSuspension T.X).DesuspendsClass (s + l) (t + l) suspendedX x →
      FiniteExtension D T.Z (.shift 1 T.X) T.h r'.toNat l s t xBar suspendedX →
      DifferentialAt D (T.Z) r (s, t)
        (s + l + n + m, t + l - 1 + n + m) xBar yBar →
      (FiniteNoCrossing D T.Z (.shift 1 T.X) T.h r'.toNat l s t ∨
        NoCrossingOn D (T.Z) r r' (s, t)) →
      FiniteExtension D T.Y T.Z T.g (m₁ + 2).toNat m (s + l + n) (t + l - 1 + n) y yBar →
      IsCycle D (T.X) (n + m + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.h) (s + l, t + l - 1) x ∧
        ∃ y' : Ambient D (T.Y) (s + l + n, t + l - 1 + n),
          FiniteExtension D T.X T.Y T.f (n + m + 1 + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower T.h).toNat
            n (s + l) (t + l - 1) x y' ∧

lean.docstring:
本文待证工具（原 am7）：MainPaper Theorem 6.12 (`thm:158d451a`) 的实际三角版本。
第二个 no-crossing 分支属于 Z 上的 d_r，在 E_r′ 页检查；不属于 g。
h 的 target 位于 ΣX，其标签通过 D.classicalSuspension 的实际 tower/layer 图和 raw-cycle
商代表元与 x 关联。该比较的构造证明尚未交付，不能以任意 E₂ 等价代替。
结论是存在同余于 y 的真实 f-extension target，模实际 B_r′；不是自由
选取的 fTarget 操作。r′ 及结论页的正性由指数和与三个长度界保证。

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:nonliftable-obstruction
entries.title: The same-quotient nonliftable obstruction
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Let $r_{\rm early}\leq r_{\rm late}$. A nonliftable obstruction is an extension of length $n-a-b$ for the normalized map in the $(r_{\rm early}-1)$-st quotient, in stem $t-s$ and weight $t+e(f)$, where
\[a,b\in\mathbb N,\qquad 0<a\leq r_{\rm early}-2,\qquad a+b\leq n.\]
Its source has filtration $s+a$ and lies outside the image of quotient reduction from the $(r_{\rm late}-1)$-st quotient on $E_\infty$; its target has filtration $s+n-b$ and is nonzero. The extension may be inessential.

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.FiniteExtensionNonliftableCrossing
lean.code:
public def FiniteExtensionNonliftableCrossing
    (rEarlier rLater : ℕ) (n s t : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ hle : rEarlier ≤ rLater, ∃ a b : ℕ,
    0 < a ∧ a ≤ rEarlier - 2 ∧ (a : ℤ) + b ≤ n ∧
    ∃ (source : ((D.family.obj ((SyntheticObject.quotient (rEarlier - 1)
          (extensionSourceObject D X Y f)).obj D.nu D.auxiliary)).sequence.ssData
          (s + a, (t - s) + (s + a), t + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f)).eInfty)
      (target : ((D.family.obj ((SyntheticObject.quotient (rEarlier - 1)
          (.nu Y)).obj D.nu D.auxiliary)).sequence.ssData
          (s + a + (n - a - b), (t - s) + (s + a + (n - a - b)),
            t + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f)).eInfty),
      source ∉ Set.range (((D.family.functor.map
        ((D.quotients.tower ((extensionSourceObject D X Y f).obj D.nu D.auxiliary)).rho
          (rEarlier - 1) (rLater - 1) (Nat.sub_le_sub_right hle 1))).eInftyMap
            (s + a, (t - s) + (s + a), t + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f)).hom) ∧
      TowerExtensionEquation (D.convergentMap
        (.quotient (rEarlier - 1) (extensionSourceObject D X Y f))
        (.quotient (rEarlier - 1) (.nu Y))
        (finiteExtensionMap D X Y f (rEarlier - 1)))
        (t - s, t + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f) (s + a) (n - a - b) source target ∧
      target ≠ 0

lean.docstring:
有限 stretching 的障碍候选，直接在同一个早期 λ 商的实际 ESS 中定义。
源和靶的 synthetic weight 固定为原 extension 的 `t + e(f)`，而源的
filtration 提高 `a`。源必须不在后期商到早期商的实际 `ρ` 所诱导的
`E∞` 映射像中；这与某个普通 Adams 代表元不属于后页 cycle 层不同。
允许 `b = 0` 及长度 `n - a - b = 0` 的 synthetic extension，包括
`e(f) = 1` 的情形。要求同商中实际 extension equation 的靶非零，不要求
essential 性，不换成较小 λ 商的 extension，也不额外施加普通 Adams
boundary 排除条件。排除这些候选强于仅排除 essential crossings；这是
修复后的充分条件，不声称与原普通 Adams 代表元谓词等价。

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-stretching-law
entries.title: The finite stretching sufficient condition
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
Suppose $2\leq r_{\rm early}\leq r_{\rm late}$ and
\[e(f)\leq n\leq r_{\rm early}-2+e(f).\]
The finite stretching law is the following implication: if
\[x\in Z_{r_{\rm late}-1}^{s,t}(X),\qquad y\in Z_{r_{\rm late}-1-n+e(f)}^{s+n,t+n}(Y),\qquad d_n^{f,E_{r_{\rm early}}}(x)=y,\]
and there is no nonliftable obstruction as above, then
\[d_n^{f,E_{r_{\rm late}}}(x)=y.\]

lean.code:
public def FinitePageExtensionStretchingLaw (X Y : ClassicalObject) (f : X.obj D.auxiliary ⟶ Y.obj D.auxiliary) : Prop :=
  ∀ (rEarlier rLater : ℕ) (n s t : ℤ)
    (x : Ambient D X (s, t)) (y : Ambient D Y (s + n, t + n)),
    2 ≤ rEarlier → rEarlier ≤ rLater →
    (normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f : ℤ) ≤ n →
    n ≤ (rEarlier : ℤ) - 2 + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f →
    IsCycle D X ((rLater : ℤ) - 1) (s, t) x →
    IsCycle D Y ((rLater : ℤ) - 1 - n + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f) (s + n, t + n) y →
    FiniteExtension D X Y f rEarlier n s t x y →
    ¬ FiniteExtensionNonliftableCrossing D X Y f rEarlier rLater n s t →
    FiniteExtension D X Y f rLater n s t x y

    (x : Ambient D X (s, t)) (y : Ambient D Y (s + n, t + n)),
    2 ≤ rEarlier → rEarlier ≤ rLater →
    (normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f : ℤ) ≤ n →
    n ≤ (rEarlier : ℤ) - 2 + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f →
    IsCycle D X ((rLater : ℤ) - 1) (s, t) x →
    IsCycle D Y ((rLater : ℤ) - 1 - n + normalizedExponent D.classicalTower f) (s + n, t + n) y →

lean.docstring:
本文待证工具（原 am7）：保留 λ 层数的有限页 stretching 充分条件。
参考 MainPaper Proposition `prop:dec738d3` 中同一有限商内的修正过程。
源、靶须属于后页所需的 cycle 层；排除的障碍是在早页同一个有限商中，
源不属于后页 ρ 的 E∞ 像、目标非零的实际较短扩张（包括非 essential 的扩张）。
不能改为只排除较小商中的无层扩张：乘 λ 可能杀掉低滤过项。
这比只排除 essential crossings 更强，不声称等价于原跨页候选或印出的推论。
原仓库已证明有限滤过修正；当前迁移状态另行追踪，不将迁移缺口认定为新假设。
结论只给出后页 extension 的存在，不声称任意指定的早期严格解可提升，
也不蕴含相容解塔或未截断 extension 的存在。

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:synthetic-boundary-labels
entries.title: Synthetic boundary maps and weighted labels
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
For $n>0$, the absolute connecting map of the quotient triangle is
\[\delta_n:
u X/\lambda^n\longrightarrow\Sigma^{1,-n}
u X.\]
For $0<n<m$, its finite version has target $\Sigma^{1,-n}(
u X/\lambda^{m-n})$. Using the suspension isomorphism of the quotient triangle, the source label of $x$ is $\lambda^a x$ in the $n$-th quotient. For a classical differential of length $r=k+1$ and $n\leq a+k$, its target label is the shifted $\lambda^{a+k-n}y$; the finite label is its image under the target quotient projection. A crossing of the absolute boundary on page $p$ is an essential extension in that same boundary ESS, with source filtration $u$ and target filtration $v$ satisfying $s<u\leq v\leq s+r$.

entries.title: Higher-source extension ranges
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body: Let $f$ be a map of convergent towers or filtered abelian groups. An extension from source filtration $s$ to target filtration $s+n$ has no higher-source crossing over $[u,s+n]$ if every extension with source filtration greater than $s$ and target filtration in $[u,s+n]$ has zero target label. All extensions, including inessential ones, occur in this quantification.

lean.code:
@[expose] public def RepresentsInfinityClass (c : SyntheticTowerConvergence P X)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s : ℤ)

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:representative-criterion
entries.title: The full representative criterion
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 2.10.)\par{}

Fix a map of convergent towers and an extension equation of length $n$ from $x$ to $y$ in filtrations $s$ and $s+n$, and a threshold $u\leq s+n$. Absence of higher-source extensions whose target lies between $u$ and $s+n$ is equivalent to the following condition: every representative $a$ of $x$ whose image has filtration at least $u$ has image representing the specified $y$ in filtration $s+n$. For threshold $u=s$, the image-filtration premise is automatic. If $y=0$, the conclusion says that every such image has filtration at least $s+n+1$. A map increasing every filtration by at least $n$ satisfies this criterion. The same assertions hold for a homomorphism of abelian groups with decreasing filtrations, using representatives of the given associated-graded source class.

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.Paper.filtered_extension_noCrossing_iff
lean.code:
public theorem filtered_extension_noCrossing_iff (f : A →+ B)
    (F : ℤ → AddSubgroup A) (G : ℤ → AddSubgroup B)
    (hF : Antitone F) (hG : Antitone G)
    (hf : ∀ u a, a ∈ F u → f a ∈ G u)
    (s n : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) (a0 : A)
    (ha0 : a0 ∈ F s) (hfa0 : f a0 ∈ G (s+n)) :
    FilteredNoCrossingRange f F G s n s ↔
      ∀ a : A, a ∈ F s → a-a0 ∈ F (s+1) →
        f a ∈ G (s+n) ∧ f a-f a0 ∈ G (s+n+1) := by
  have h := filtered_extension_noCrossingRange_iff f F G hF hG hf s n s (by omega) a0 ha0 hfa0
  constructor
  · intro hc a ha hd
    exact h.mp hc a ha hd (hf s a ha)
  · intro hall
    exact h.mpr (fun a ha hd _ => hall a ha hd)

lean.code:
public theorem filtered_extension_noCrossingRange_iff (f : A →+ B)
    (F : ℤ → AddSubgroup A) (G : ℤ → AddSubgroup B)
    (hF : Antitone F) (hG : Antitone G)
    (hf : ∀ u a, a ∈ F u → f a ∈ G u)
    (s n threshold : ℤ) (ht : threshold ≤ s+n)
    (a0 : A) (ha0 : a0 ∈ F s) (hfa0 : f a0 ∈ G (s+n)) :
    FilteredNoCrossingRange f F G s n threshold ↔
      ∀ a : A, a ∈ F s → a-a0 ∈ F (s+1) → f a ∈ G threshold →
        f a ∈ G (s+n) ∧ f a-f a0 ∈ G (s+n+1) := by
  constructor
  · intro hc a _ hd hfa
    have hh := filtered_correction_in_next f F G hG hf s n threshold ht hc
      (a-a0) hd (by rw [map_sub]; exact (G threshold).sub_mem hfa (hG ht hfa0))
    have hdiff : f a-f a0 ∈ G (s+n+1) := by simpa only [map_sub] using hh
    refine ⟨?_,hdiff⟩
    have h := (G (s+n)).add_mem (hG (show s+n ≤ s+n+1 by omega) hdiff) hfa0
    simpa only [sub_add_cancel] using h
  · intro hall u v hsu huv htv hvs a ha hfa
    have ha' : a ∈ F (s+1) := hF (by omega) ha
    have hsum : a0+a ∈ F s := (F s).add_mem ha0 (hF (by omega) ha)
    have hdiff : a0+a-a0 ∈ F (s+1) := by simpa only [add_sub_cancel_left] using ha'
    have hsumf : f (a0+a) ∈ G threshold := by
      rw [map_add]
      exact (G threshold).add_mem (hG ht hfa0) (hG htv hfa)
    have hh := (hall (a0+a) hsum hdiff hsumf).2
    have hh' : f a ∈ G (s+n+1) := by simpa only [map_add,add_sub_cancel_left] using hh
    exact hG (by omega) hh'

labels is a-a0 ∈ F^(s+1); equality of target labels is f(a)-f(a0) ∈ G^(s+n+1).
Thus this formulation applies to classical homotopy groups as well as to the
synthetic representative version above.  a0 is a witness of the given extension.

lean.code:
public theorem extension_noCrossingRange_iff
    (M : ConvergentMap E g cx.toConvergence cy.toConvergence)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s n threshold : ℤ) (hthreshold : threshold ≤ s+n)
    (x : ((E.obj X).sequence.ssData (s,p.1+s,p.2)).eInfty)
    (y : ((E.obj Y).sequence.ssData (s+n,p.1+(s+n),p.2)).eInfty)
    (he : TowerExtensionEquation M p s n x y) :
    ExtensionNoCrossingRange M p s n threshold ↔
      ∀ a : BiHom p.1 p.2 X, RepresentsInfinityClass cx p s x a →
        a ≫ g ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule Y threshold p →
        RepresentsInfinityClass cy p (s+n) y (a ≫ g) := by
  obtain ⟨hn,ar₀,br₀,he₀,hx₀,hy₀⟩ := (tower_extension_iff M p s n x y).mp he
  let a₀ : BiHom p.1 p.2 X := ((P.filtration X).F s p).arrow ar₀
  let b₀ : BiHom p.1 p.2 Y := ((P.filtration Y).F (s+n) p).arrow br₀
  have hx : RepresentsInfinityClass cx p s x a₀ := ⟨ar₀,rfl,hx₀⟩
  have hy : RepresentsInfinityClass cy p (s+n) y b₀ := ⟨br₀,rfl,hy₀⟩
  have hbase : a₀ ≫ g = b₀ := he₀
  constructor
  · intro hc a ha hga
    have hdiff := representatives_difference p s x a a₀ ha hx
    have himage : (a-a₀) ≫ g ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule Y threshold p := by
      rw [Preadditive.sub_comp,hbase]
      exact (P.filtrationSubmodule Y threshold p).sub_mem hga
        (P.filtrationSubmodule_antitone Y p hthreshold (represents_mem p (s+n) y b₀ hy))
    have hh := image_correction_in_next M p s n threshold hthreshold hc (a-a₀) hdiff himage
    apply represents_of_difference p (s+n) y (a≫g) b₀ hy
    simpa only [Preadditive.sub_comp,hbase] using hh
  · intro hall u v hsu huv htv hvs xx yy he'
    obtain ⟨_,ar,br,heq,hxx,hyy⟩ := (tower_extension_iff M p u (v-u) xx yy).mp he'
    let a : BiHom p.1 p.2 X := ((P.filtration X).F u p).arrow ar
    have ha : a ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule X u p := by
      have h : a ∈ ModuleCat.subobjectModule _ ((P.filtration X).F u p) := ⟨ar,rfl⟩
      simpa only [SyntheticTowerPresentation.filtration,OrderIso.apply_symm_apply] using h
    have hfa : a≫g ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule Y v p := by
      have h : a≫g ∈ ModuleCat.subobjectModule _ ((P.filtration Y).F (u+(v-u)) p) :=
        ⟨br,heq.symm⟩
      simpa only [SyntheticTowerPresentation.filtration,OrderIso.apply_symm_apply,
        add_sub_cancel] using h
    have hsum : RepresentsInfinityClass cx p s x (a₀+a) := by
      apply represents_of_difference p s x (a₀+a) a₀ hx
      simpa only [add_sub_cancel_left] using
        (P.filtrationSubmodule_antitone X p (show s+1 ≤ u by omega) ha)
    have hsumg : (a₀+a)≫g ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule Y threshold p := by
      rw [Preadditive.add_comp,hbase]
      exact (P.filtrationSubmodule Y threshold p).add_mem
        (P.filtrationSubmodule_antitone Y p hthreshold (represents_mem p (s+n) y b₀ hy))
        (P.filtrationSubmodule_antitone Y p htv hfa)
    have hdet := hall (a₀+a) hsum hsumg
    have hdiff := representatives_difference p (s+n) y ((a₀+a)≫g) b₀ hdet hy
    have hnext : a≫g ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule Y (v+1) p := by
      have h : a≫g ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule Y (s+n+1) p := by
        simpa only [Preadditive.add_comp,hbase,add_sub_cancel_left] using hdiff
      exact P.filtrationSubmodule_antitone Y p (by omega) h
    have hzero := (Internal.element_grade_equal_iff (P.filtration Y) (u+(v-u)) p br 0).mpr
      (by
        rw [←heq,map_zero,sub_zero]
        simpa only [SyntheticTowerPresentation.filtration,OrderIso.apply_symm_apply,
          add_sub_cancel, a] using hnext)
    apply (ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective (infinityGradedIso cy p (u+(v-u))).hom).mp inferInstance
    rw [map_zero]
    rw [map_zero] at hzero
  -- … (truncated)

    (M : ConvergentMap E g cx.toConvergence cy.toConvergence)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s n threshold : ℤ) (hthreshold : threshold ≤ s+n)
    (x : ((E.obj X).sequence.ssData (s,p.1+s,p.2)).eInfty)
    (y : ((E.obj Y).sequence.ssData (s+n,p.1+(s+n),p.2)).eInfty)

public theorem extension_noCrossing_of_filtration_bound
    (M : ConvergentMap E g cx.toConvergence cy.toConvergence)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s n : ℤ)
    (x : ((E.obj X).sequence.ssData (s,p.1+s,p.2)).eInfty)
    (y : ((E.obj Y).sequence.ssData (s+n,p.1+(s+n),p.2)).eInfty)
    (he : TowerExtensionEquation M p s n x y)
    (hmap : ∀ k : ℤ, ∀ a : BiHom p.1 p.2 X,
      a ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule X k p →
      a ≫ g ∈ P.filtrationSubmodule Y (k+n) p) :
    ExtensionNoCrossingRange M p s n s := by
  apply (extension_noCrossing_iff M p s n x y he).mpr
  obtain ⟨_,ar₀,br₀,he₀,hx₀,hy₀⟩ := (tower_extension_iff M p s n x y).mp he
  let a₀ : BiHom p.1 p.2 X := ((P.filtration X).F s p).arrow ar₀
  let b₀ : BiHom p.1 p.2 Y := ((P.filtration Y).F (s+n) p).arrow br₀
  have hx : RepresentsInfinityClass cx p s x a₀ := ⟨ar₀,rfl,hx₀⟩
  have hy : RepresentsInfinityClass cy p (s+n) y b₀ := ⟨br₀,rfl,hy₀⟩
  have hbase : a₀ ≫ g = b₀ := he₀
  intro a ha
  apply represents_of_difference p (s+n) y (a≫g) b₀ hy
  have hdiff := hmap (s+1) (a-a₀) (representatives_difference p s x a a₀ ha hx)
  simpa only [Preadditive.sub_comp,hbase,add_assoc,add_comm,add_left_comm] using hdiff

public theorem extension_noCrossing_iff
    (M : ConvergentMap E g cx.toConvergence cy.toConvergence)
    (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s n : ℤ)

entries.title: Finite correction labels
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body: For $f:X\to Y$ and $x'\in E_2^{s+a,t+a}(X)$, the finite correction label is the image of $\lambda^a x'$ under the shift comparison and quotient isomorphism into the normalized finite source quotient, in synthetic weight $t+e(f)$.

    (x : Ambient model X (s+a,(t-s)+(s+a))) :
    (model.family.obj ((SyntheticObject.quotient q (extensionSourceObject model X Y f)).obj
      model.nu model.auxiliary)).E₂

  familyPageMap model.family (correctionShiftIso X Y f q).inv 2 _
    (regradeE2 (by ext <;> dsimp <;> omega)

        (.quotient q (.nu X)) 2 (by decide)

entries.label: sem:ProofTools:nonliftable-or-crossing
entries.title: A nonliftable short extension or a late crossing
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body: Consider finite witnesses for the same $f,x,y,n$ on pages $r_{\rm early}\leq r_{\rm late}$. If the late witness is essential and the early one is inessential, then either a shorter early extension retains the original target and has a source in the earlier cycle set but outside the later cycle set, or the same late normalized extension spectral sequence has a nonzero higher-source crossing in the specified range. The first branch uses the actual correction label with $b=0$ and all length and cycle bounds.

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.Paper.FiniteExtensionNonliftableShortTo
lean.code:
@[expose] public def FiniteExtensionNonliftableShortTo (X Y : ClassicalObject)
    (f : X.obj model.auxiliary ⟶ Y.obj model.auxiliary)
    (rEarlier rLater : ℕ) (n s t : ℤ) (x y)
    (Wearly : FiniteExtensionWitness model X Y f rEarlier n s t x y) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ (a:ℤ) ≤ n-normalizedExponent model.classicalTower f ∧
    ∃ x' : Ambient model X (s+a,(t-s)+(s+a)),
      x' ∈ cycles model X (((rEarlier-1:ℕ):ℤ)-a) (s+a,(t-s)+(s+a)) ∧
      x' ∉ cycles model X (((rLater-1:ℕ):ℤ)-a) (s+a,(t-s)+(s+a)) ∧
      ∃ z,
        HasInfinityRepresentative _ 2 _
          (finiteExtensionCorrectionLabel X Y f (rEarlier-1) s t a x') z ∧
        TowerExtensionEquation (model.convergentMap
          (.quotient (rEarlier-1) (extensionSourceObject model X Y f))
          (.quotient (rEarlier-1) (.nu Y)) (finiteExtensionMap model X Y f (rEarlier-1)))
          (t-s,t+normalizedExponent model.classicalTower f) (s+a) (n-a) z
          ((eqToHom (congrArg (fun d =>
            ((model.family.obj ((SyntheticObject.quotient (rEarlier-1) (.nu Y)).obj
              model.nu model.auxiliary)).sequence.ssData
              (d,(t-s)+d,t+normalizedExponent model.classicalTower f)).eInfty)
            (show s+n = (s+a)+(n-a) by omega))) Wearly.target)

lean.code:
public theorem finiteExtension_nonliftableShort_or_lateCrossing (X Y : ClassicalObject)
    (f : X.obj model.auxiliary ⟶ Y.obj model.auxiliary)
    (rEarlier rLater : ℕ) (n s t : ℤ) (x y)
    (Wlater : FiniteExtensionWitness model X Y f rLater n s t x y)
    (Wearly : FiniteExtensionWitness model X Y f rEarlier n s t x y)
    (hle : rEarlier ≤ rLater) (hess : Wlater.Essential) (hne : ¬Wearly.Essential) :
    FiniteExtensionNonliftableShortTo X Y f rEarlier rLater n s t x y Wearly ∨
      ¬ ExtensionNoCrossingRange (model.convergentMap
        (.quotient (rLater-1) (extensionSourceObject model X Y f))
        (.quotient (rLater-1) (.nu Y)) (finiteExtensionMap model X Y f (rLater-1)))
        (t-s,t+normalizedExponent model.classicalTower f) s n s := by
  classical
  by_cases hc : ExtensionNoCrossingRange (model.convergentMap
      (.quotient (rLater-1) (extensionSourceObject model X Y f))
      (.quotient (rLater-1) (.nu Y)) (finiteExtensionMap model X Y f (rLater-1)))
      (t-s,t+normalizedExponent model.classicalTower f) s n s
  · have hy := earlier_target_nonzero X Y f rEarlier rLater n s t x y Wlater Wearly hle hess
    obtain ⟨a,ha,han,x',hx',z,hz,hs⟩ := finiteExtension_essential_shorter_source
      X Y f rEarlier n s t x y Wearly hy hne
    by_cases hxl : x'∈cycles model X (((rLater-1:ℕ):ℤ)-a) (s+a,(t-s)+(s+a))
    · have hi : 0<rEarlier-1 := by have := Wearly.page_ge_two; omega
      have haq : a<rEarlier-1 := by have := Wearly.length_upper; omega
      obtain ⟨zl,hzl⟩ := correction_source_lift_of_late_cycle X Y f
        (rEarlier-1) (rLater-1) hi (Nat.sub_le_sub_right hle 1) s t a haq x' hxl z hz
      apply False.elim
      exact essential_short_source_not_in_range
        (.quotient (rLater-1) (extensionSourceObject model X Y f))
        (.quotient (rLater-1) (.nu Y))
        (.quotient (rEarlier-1) (extensionSourceObject model X Y f))
        (.quotient (rEarlier-1) (.nu Y))
        (finiteExtensionMap model X Y f (rLater-1))
        (finiteExtensionMap model X Y f (rEarlier-1))
        ((model.quotients.tower ((extensionSourceObject model X Y f).obj model.nu model.auxiliary)).rho
          (rEarlier-1) (rLater-1) (Nat.sub_le_sub_right hle 1))
        ((model.quotients.tower (model.nu.functor.obj (Y.obj model.auxiliary))).rho
          (rEarlier-1) (rLater-1) (Nat.sub_le_sub_right hle 1))
        ((model.quotients.natural (model.normalizedMap X Y f).map).rho_naturality
          (Nat.sub_le_sub_right hle 1))
        (t-s,t+normalizedExponent model.classicalTower f) s n (s+a) (n-a)
        (by have := Wearly.length_lower; omega) (by omega) (by omega) hc z _ hs zl hzl
    · exact Or.inl ⟨a,ha,han,x',hx',hxl,z,hz,hs.1⟩
  · exact Or.inr hc

(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 2.7.)


\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)] For $x\in E_\infty^{s,t}(X)$, we say that the an $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ has a crossing that hits Adams filtration $p$ for some $p \leq s+n$, if there exists an element $x^\prime\in E_\infty^{s+a,t+a}(X)$ with $a>0$ and an $f$-extension $d_m^{f}(x^\prime)=y^\prime$ for $0\neq y^\prime\in E^{s+a+m, t+a+m}_\infty(Y)$ such that
    $$p = \textup{AF}(y^\prime) = s+a+m\le \textup{AF}(y) = s+n.$$
    \item[(2)] We say that an $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ has no crossing that hits the range AF $\ge p$ if there does not exist an element $x^\prime\in E_\infty^{s+a,t+a}(X)$ with $a>0$ and an $f$-extension $d_m^{f}(x^\prime)=y^\prime$ for $0\neq y^\prime\in E^{s+a+m, t+a+m}_\infty(Y)$ such that
    $$p\le \textup{AF}(y^\prime) = s+a+m\le \textup{AF}(y) = s+n.$$
    \item[(3)] We say that an $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ has no crossing if it has no crossing that hits the range AF$\ge \AF(x) + 1$.
\end{enumerate}

entries.label: paper:2.10
entries.title: Characterization of extensions without crossings
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 2.10.)


    An $f$-extension from $x$ to $y$ has no crossing in the range $\AF\ge p$ if and only if for all $[x]\in \{x\}$ such that $\AF(f[x])\ge p$ we have $f[x]\in \{y\}$. In particular, we have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] An $f$-extension from $x$ to $y$ has no crossing if and only if for all $[x]\in \{x\}$ we have $f[x]\in \{y\}$.
        \item[(2)] An $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=0$ has no crossing if and only if for all $[x]\in \{x\}$,
        $$\AF(f[x]) >\AF(x)+n.$$
        \item[(3)] If $\AF(f)=n$, then all $d^f_n$-differentials have no crossing in the $f$-ESS.
    \end{enumerate}

lean.name: KIP126.ProofTools.Paper.filtered_extension_noCrossing_iff
lean.code:
public theorem filtered_extension_noCrossing_iff (f : A →+ B)
    (F : ℤ → AddSubgroup A) (G : ℤ → AddSubgroup B)
    (hF : Antitone F) (hG : Antitone G)
    (hf : ∀ u a, a ∈ F u → f a ∈ G u)
    (s n : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) (a0 : A)
    (ha0 : a0 ∈ F s) (hfa0 : f a0 ∈ G (s+n)) :
    FilteredNoCrossingRange f F G s n s ↔
      ∀ a : A, a ∈ F s → a-a0 ∈ F (s+1) →
        f a ∈ G (s+n) ∧ f a-f a0 ∈ G (s+n+1) := by
  have h := filtered_extension_noCrossingRange_iff f F G hF hG hf s n s (by omega) a0 ha0 hfa0
  constructor
  · intro hc a ha hd
    exact h.mp hc a ha hd (hf s a ha)
  · intro hall
    exact h.mpr (fun a ha hd _ => hall a ha hd)

lean.code:
public theorem filtered_extension_noCrossingRange_iff (f : A →+ B)
    (F : ℤ → AddSubgroup A) (G : ℤ → AddSubgroup B)
    (hF : Antitone F) (hG : Antitone G)
    (hf : ∀ u a, a ∈ F u → f a ∈ G u)
    (s n threshold : ℤ) (ht : threshold ≤ s+n)
    (a0 : A) (ha0 : a0 ∈ F s) (hfa0 : f a0 ∈ G (s+n)) :
    FilteredNoCrossingRange f F G s n threshold ↔
      ∀ a : A, a ∈ F s → a-a0 ∈ F (s+1) → f a ∈ G threshold →
        f a ∈ G (s+n) ∧ f a-f a0 ∈ G (s+n+1) := by
  constructor
  · intro hc a _ hd hfa
    have hh := filtered_correction_in_next f F G hG hf s n threshold ht hc
      (a-a0) hd (by rw [map_sub]; exact (G threshold).sub_mem hfa (hG ht hfa0))
    have hdiff : f a-f a0 ∈ G (s+n+1) := by simpa only [map_sub] using hh
    refine ⟨?_,hdiff⟩
    have h := (G (s+n)).add_mem (hG (show s+n ≤ s+n+1 by omega) hdiff) hfa0
    simpa only [sub_add_cancel] using h
  · intro hall u v hsu huv htv hvs a ha hfa
    have ha' : a ∈ F (s+1) := hF (by omega) ha
    have hsum : a0+a ∈ F s := (F s).add_mem ha0 (hF (by omega) ha)
    have hdiff : a0+a-a0 ∈ F (s+1) := by simpa only [add_sub_cancel_left] using ha'
    have hsumf : f (a0+a) ∈ G threshold := by
      rw [map_add]
      exact (G threshold).add_mem (hG ht hfa0) (hG htv hfa)
    have hh := (hall (a0+a) hsum hdiff hsumf).2
    have hh' : f a ∈ G (s+n+1) := by simpa only [map_add,add_sub_cancel_left] using hh
    exact hG (by omega) hh'

entries.title: The extension theorem for a commutative square
entries.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entries.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorem 2.12.)


    Consider a homotopy commutative diagram of spectra
    $$\text{see the original commutative diagram}$$
    Suppose $m,n,l\ge 0$, $0<k\le m+l-n$,
    $$\begin{array}{ll}
        x\in E^{s,t}_\infty(X) & y\in E^{s+n,t+n}_\infty(Y),\\
        z\in E^{s+m,t+m}_\infty(Z) & w\in E^{s+m+l,t+m+l}_\infty(W),
    \end{array}$$
    and
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $d^{f}_{n}(x)=y$,
        \item[(2)] $d^{p}_{m}(x)=z$,
        \item[(3)] the differential in (1) or the differential in (2) has no crossing,
        \item[(4)] $d^{g}_{l}(z)=w$, and has no crossing that hits the range AF $\ge s+n+k$,
        \item[(5)] $d^{q}_{k-1} y=0$, and has no crossing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $d^{q}_{m+l-n}(y)=w$. (See Figure \href{paper/main.tex.html#L551}{original source}.)
\par\href{paper/diagrams/2.12.html}{Original diagrams and hypotheses}
